manifest.title: First-Order Model Checking on Monadically Dependent Graph Classes

inputs.abstract:
Monadically dependent graph classes are those in which first-order logic cannot
encode all graphs. They include all nowhere dense classes and all classes of
bounded twin-width.

We show that first-order model checking is fixed-parameter tractable on every
monadically dependent graph class. Together with the known hardness result for
hereditary classes that are not monadically dependent, this gives a complete
characterization of the hereditary graph classes with fixed-parameter tractable
first-order model checking. This resolves a central open problem in algorithmic
model theory.

Our proof combines ideas from structural graph theory (graph decompositions),
finite model theory (locality of first-order logic), and model theory (counting
types). In particular, we show that in monadically dependent classes, tuples of
fixed length have only $|U|^{O(1)}$ types of fixed quantifier rank over any set
of parameters $U$.

concepts.title: Algorithms and their running times
concepts.description:
An *algorithm* is a program of the word RAM of `Lax808846.Ram`. It reads
the encoding of a value and writes the encoding of a value, in the
encodings of `Lax185574.Encoding`.

The word RAM computes with words of w bits. As usual, the word length
must grow logarithmically with the input, so that a word can hold an
address of the input and each number of the input. Each algorithm states
how much it needs: an exponent e such that it works with words of
e · log₂ (N + Σ) + O(1) bits on inputs of length N whose numbers sum to
Σ.

The algorithm A *computes* b from a *in time O(T)*, with the constant c,
if the following holds for the encoding x of a, of length N, whose
numbers sum to Σ. At every word length w with c · (N + Σ + 1)^e ≤ 2^w,

1. every run of A on x that halts outputs the encoding of b, and
2. if c · T + c ≤ 2^w, then A halts on x within c · T + c steps.

A word length w with c · (N + Σ + 1)^e ≤ 2^w is called *admissible* for
c on the input x.

The algorithm A *decides* a property P of a in time O(T) if it computes
the truth value of P in time O(T).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A statement about an algorithm has the form "there is an algorithm A
such that for all parameters there is a constant c such that for all
inputs a, A computes b from a in time O(T)". The program and the
exponent e come first, so neither depends on the parameters or on the
word length. The constant c is O-notation with explicit constants. It
bounds both the running time and the additive term of the word length.

The word length bound includes the numbers of the input, since the
machine reduces every number modulo 2^w, so a number that does not fit
into a word cannot be read. The sum of the numbers dominates each of
them and also covers the empty input.

The first clause is soundness at every word length of the hypothesis.
An algorithm that calls another one runs it at word lengths fixed by its
own memory, where the running time of the callee need not fit into a
word. It can trust any output it receives. The second clause claims
halting only once the time bound fits into a word, the usual word RAM
convention that a word holds the running time. This matters when the
output is large. Its size can be polynomial of a degree that grows with
parameters fixed after e, and then at some word lengths of the
hypothesis the output cannot be written. Since the machine is
deterministic, the two clauses together say that the run is correct
whenever it halts, and that it halts in time whenever the time fits.

The time bound is a real number, so that bounds like n^(3+ε) can be
written directly. The additive c lets T vanish on small inputs, as
O-notation does. Several outputs are computed as one pair.

import Lax185574.Encodings
import Lax808846.Ram
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

/-!

title: Algorithms and their running times
type: definition

namespace Lax185574.Algorithms

open Lax808846.Ram Lax185574.Encoding

/-- An algorithm: a word RAM program, together with the exponent `e`
such that it needs words of `e · log₂ (N + Σ) + O(1)` bits on inputs of
length `N` whose numbers sum to `Σ`. -/
structure Algorithm where
  /-- The program. -/
  program : Program
  /-- The exponent of the word length the algorithm needs. -/
  wordExponent : ℕ

/-- `A.Computes c a b T`: the algorithm `A` computes `b` from `a` in time
`O(T)`, with the constant `c`. Let `x` be the encoding of `a`. At every
word length `w` with `c · (|x| + Σx + 1)^e ≤ 2^w`, where `Σx` is the sum
of the numbers of `x`,
1. every halting run of `A` on `x` outputs the encoding of `b`, and
2. if `c · T + c ≤ 2^w`, then `A` halts on `x` within `c · T + c` steps,
   with the encoding of `b` as output. -/
def Algorithm.Computes {α β : Type*} [Encode α] [Encode β]
    (A : Algorithm) (c : ℕ) (a : α) (b : β) (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ w : ℕ, c * ((encode a).length + (encode a).sum + 1) ^ A.wordExponent ≤ 2 ^ w →
    (∀ y t, RunsTo w A.program (encode a) y t → y = encode b) ∧
    ((c : ℝ) * T + c ≤ 2 ^ w →
      ∃ t : ℕ, (t : ℝ) ≤ c * T + c ∧ RunsTo w A.program (encode a) (encode b) t)

open Classical in
/-- `A.Decides c a P T`: the algorithm `A` computes from `a` whether `P`
holds, writing `true` (encoded as `1`) or `false` (encoded as `0`), in
time `O(T)` with the constant `c`. -/
def Algorithm.Decides {α : Type*} [Encode α] (A : Algorithm) (c : ℕ) (a : α) (P : Prop)
    (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  A.Computes c a (decide P) T

end Lax185574.Algorithms

concepts.title: Atomically matched tuples
concepts.description:
For a graph G and tuples ā, b̄ ∈ V(G)^t, the tuples ā = a₁ … a_t and
b̄ = b₁ … b_t are *atomically matched* if there is a relation
∼ ∈ {=, ≠, ≥} such that G ⊨ E(aᵢ, bⱼ) if and only if i ∼ j, for all
i, j ∈ [t]. In particular, the bipartite graph semi-induced between the
tuples ā and b̄ is a matching, a co-matching, or a half-graph.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Positions are `Fin t`, which is [t] shifted by one and carries the same
order. The relation i ≥ j is written j ≤ i. Only the adjacency between
the entries of ā and the entries of b̄ is constrained. The entries need
not be distinct, although the conditions force some distinctness, for
instance aᵢ ≠ bᵢ in the case of =.

import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
import Mathlib.Order.Fin.Basic

/-!
---
title: Atomically matched tuples
type: definition
---
For a graph G and tuples ā, b̄ ∈ V(G)^t, the tuples ā = a₁ … a_t and
b̄ = b₁ … b_t are *atomically matched* if there is a relation
∼ ∈ {=, ≠, ≥} such that G ⊨ E(aᵢ, bⱼ) if and only if i ∼ j, for all
i, j ∈ [t]. In particular, the bipartite graph semi-induced between the
tuples ā and b̄ is a matching, a co-matching, or a half-graph.

# Formalization notes

Positions are `Fin t`, which is [t] shifted by one and carries the same
order. The relation i ≥ j is written j ≤ i. Only the adjacency between
the entries of ā and the entries of b̄ is constrained. The entries need
not be distinct, although the conditions force some distinctness, for
instance aᵢ ≠ bᵢ in the case of =.
-/

namespace Lax185574.AtomicMatching

universe u

variable {V : Type u}

/-- The tuples `a` and `b` are atomically matched in `G`: adjacency of
`a i` and `b j` is described by `i = j`, by `i ≠ j`, or by `i ≥ j`. -/
def AtomicallyMatched (G : SimpleGraph V) {t : ℕ} (a b : Fin t → V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j, G.Adj (a i) (b j) ↔ i = j) ∨
  (∀ i j, G.Adj (a i) (b j) ↔ i ≠ j) ∨
  (∀ i j, G.Adj (a i) (b j) ↔ j ≤ i)

end Lax185574.AtomicMatching

concepts.title: Atomic types of vertices and of pairs
concepts.description:
The *atomic type* of a tuple v̄ over a set Y of elements of a structure A
is atp^A(v̄/Y) ≔ tp^A_0(v̄/Y), and ATypes^A(X/Y) ≔ Types^A_{1,0}(X/Y) is
the set of atomic types over Y of the elements of X.

For a graph, Π = {(x = y), (x ≠ y) ∧ E(x, y), (x ≠ y) ∧ ¬E(x, y)} is the
set of the three possible atomic types of a pair of vertices. For an
s-tuple p̄ = (p₁, …, p_s) of vertices and a vertex v, the atomic type
atp(v/p̄) is identified with the s-tuple in Π^s whose i-th component is
the atomic type of the pair (v, pᵢ).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The number |ATypes^G(X/Y)| is `atomicTypeCount`. It is literally the
number of types of quantifier rank 0 of single vertices of X over Y in
the structure of the graph G, as defined in `FirstOrderTypes`.

The three atomic types of a pair form the type `PairType`, and
atp(v/p̄) is `atomicTypeOver G p v`. The partition 𝒫_S of V(G) into
atomic types over a set S is `Partitions.atomicTypes`. Two vertices have
the same atomic type over a tuple p̄ exactly when they lie in the same
part of 𝒫_S for the set S of entries of p̄.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax185574.FirstOrderTypes
import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Graph

/-!
---
title: Atomic types of vertices and of pairs
type: definition
---
The *atomic type* of a tuple v̄ over a set Y of elements of a structure A
is atp^A(v̄/Y) ≔ tp^A_0(v̄/Y), and ATypes^A(X/Y) ≔ Types^A_{1,0}(X/Y) is
the set of atomic types over Y of the elements of X.

For a graph, Π = {(x = y), (x ≠ y) ∧ E(x, y), (x ≠ y) ∧ ¬E(x, y)} is the
set of the three possible atomic types of a pair of vertices. For an
s-tuple p̄ = (p₁, …, p_s) of vertices and a vertex v, the atomic type
atp(v/p̄) is identified with the s-tuple in Π^s whose i-th component is
the atomic type of the pair (v, pᵢ).

# Formalization notes

The number |ATypes^G(X/Y)| is `atomicTypeCount`. It is literally the
number of types of quantifier rank 0 of single vertices of X over Y in
the structure of the graph G, as defined in `FirstOrderTypes`.

The three atomic types of a pair form the type `PairType`, and
atp(v/p̄) is `atomicTypeOver G p v`. The partition 𝒫_S of V(G) into
atomic types over a set S is `Partitions.atomicTypes`. Two vertices have
the same atomic type over a tuple p̄ exactly when they lie in the same
part of 𝒫_S for the set S of entries of p̄.
-/

namespace Lax185574.AtomicTypes

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language
open Lax185574.FirstOrderTypes

universe u

variable {V : Type u}

/-- `|ATypes^G(X/Y)|`: the number of atomic types over `Y`, in the graph
`G`, of the vertices of `X`. -/
noncomputable def atomicTypeCount (G : SimpleGraph V) (X Y : Set V) : ℕ :=
  @typeCountOver Language.graph V G.structure 1 0 X Y

/-- The three atomic types of a pair of vertices in a graph, the set Π. -/
inductive PairType
  /-- The type `x = y`. -/
  | eq
  /-- The type `x ≠ y ∧ E(x, y)`. -/
  | adj
  /-- The type `x ≠ y ∧ ¬E(x, y)`. -/
  | nonAdj
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- There are three atomic types of pairs. -/
instance : Fintype PairType :=
  ⟨{.eq, .adj, .nonAdj}, fun x => by cases x <;> decide⟩

open Classical in
/-- The atomic type of the pair `(u, v)` in the graph `G`. -/
noncomputable def pairType (G : SimpleGraph V) (u v : V) : PairType :=
  if u = v then .eq else if G.Adj u v then .adj else .nonAdj

/-- `atp(v/p̄)`, as an element of `Π^s`: its `i`-th component is the
atomic type of the pair `(v, pᵢ)`. -/
noncomputable def atomicTypeOver (G : SimpleGraph V) {s : ℕ} (p : Fin s → V)
    (v : V) : Fin s → PairType :=
  fun i => pairType G v (p i)

end Lax185574.AtomicTypes

concepts.title: A definable flip separating a ball one step further
concepts.description:
For all d, t ∈ ℕ, there is some z ∈ ℕ with the following property.

For every graph G of VC-dimension at most d, radius r ∈ ℕ, finite set
A ⊆ V(G), and arbitrary set C ⊆ V(G) satisfying

Ball^G_r[C] ∩ A = ∅  and  |ATypes^G(Ball^G_r[C]/A)| ≤ t,

there exists a z-definable flip H of G in which Ball^H_{r+1}[C] ∩ A = ∅.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The number z is chosen after d and t and before the graph and the
radius, so it does not depend on r. The graph is finite, so A is finite.
The paper also allows infinite graphs with A finite. The lemma is
applied in the proof of the closure theorem to flips of graphs of a
graph class, which are finite. The atomic types are taken in G.

import Lax185574.AtomicTypes
import Lax185574.DefinableFlips
import Lax185574.GraphBalls
import Lax185574.VCDimension

/-!
---
title: A definable flip separating a ball one step further
type: lemma
---
For all d, t ∈ ℕ, there is some z ∈ ℕ with the following property.

For every graph G of VC-dimension at most d, radius r ∈ ℕ, finite set
A ⊆ V(G), and arbitrary set C ⊆ V(G) satisfying

Ball^G_r[C] ∩ A = ∅  and  |ATypes^G(Ball^G_r[C]/A)| ≤ t,

there exists a z-definable flip H of G in which Ball^H_{r+1}[C] ∩ A = ∅.

# Formalization notes

The number z is chosen after d and t and before the graph and the
radius, so it does not depend on r. The graph is finite, so A is finite.
The paper also allows infinite graphs with A finite. The lemma is
applied in the proof of the closure theorem to flips of graphs of a
graph class, which are finite. The atomic types are taken in G.
-/

namespace Lax185574.BallFlip

open Lax185574.AtomicTypes Lax185574.DefinableFlips Lax185574.GraphBalls
open Lax185574.VCDimension

universe u

/-- **Ball flip.** If a ball of radius `r` around `C` avoids `A` and
realizes at most `t` atomic types over `A`, then a `z(d, t)`-definable
flip moves `A` out of the ball of radius `r + 1` around `C`. -/
axiom exists_ball_flip (d t : ℕ) :
    ∃ z : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type u) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V), vcDim G ≤ d →
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (A C : Set V), Disjoint (graphBall G r C) A →
        atomicTypeCount G (graphBall G r C) A ≤ t →
        ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, IsDefinableFlip G z H ∧
          Disjoint (graphBall H (r + 1) C) A

end Lax185574.BallFlip

statements.signature:
exists_ball_flip : ∀ (d t : Nat),
  Exists fun z =>
    ∀ (V : Type u) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      instLEENat.le (Lax185574.VCDimension.vcDim G) d.cast →
        ∀ (r : Nat) (A C : Set V),
          Disjoint (Lax185574.GraphBalls.graphBall G r C) A →
            instLENat.le (Lax185574.AtomicTypes.atomicTypeCount G (Lax185574.GraphBalls.graphBall G r C) A) t →
              Exists fun H =>
                And (Lax185574.DefinableFlips.IsDefinableFlip G z H)
                  (Disjoint (Lax185574.GraphBalls.graphBall H (instHAdd.hAdd r 1) C) A)

**Ball flip.** If a ball of radius `r` around `C` avoids `A` and
realizes at most `t` atomic types over `A`, then a `z(d, t)`-definable
flip moves `A` out of the ball of radius `r + 1` around `C`.

concepts.title: Few atomic types in balls avoiding a closure
concepts.description:
For every monadically dependent graph class 𝒞 and r, s ∈ ℕ, there are
some k, t ∈ ℕ with the following property. For every G ∈ 𝒞 and finite
set A ⊆ V(G), there is A* ⊇ A of size O_{𝒞,r,s}(|A|^k) such that, for
every s-definable flip H of G and every vertex v,

Ball^H_r[v] ∩ A* = ∅  ⟹  |ATypes^H(Ball^H_r[v]/A)| ≤ t.

Equivalently, Ball^H_r[v] intersects at most t parts of the partition of
V(H) into atomic types over A in H.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The bound O_{𝒞,r,s}(|A|^k) is spelled out as a · (|A| + 1)^k, with a
chosen together with k and t, after 𝒞, r and s. The set A* is chosen
before the flip H and the vertex v. The atomic types are taken in the
flip H, as in the paper. The parameter bound s is an input of the lemma,
not an output. The graphs of 𝒞 are finite, as in `ClosureTheorem`.

import Lax185574.AtomicTypes
import Lax185574.DefinableFlips
import Lax185574.GraphBalls
import Lax185574.MonadicDependence

/-!
---
title: Few atomic types in balls avoiding a closure
type: lemma
---
For every monadically dependent graph class 𝒞 and r, s ∈ ℕ, there are
some k, t ∈ ℕ with the following property. For every G ∈ 𝒞 and finite
set A ⊆ V(G), there is A* ⊇ A of size O_{𝒞,r,s}(|A|^k) such that, for
every s-definable flip H of G and every vertex v,

Ball^H_r[v] ∩ A* = ∅  ⟹  |ATypes^H(Ball^H_r[v]/A)| ≤ t.

Equivalently, Ball^H_r[v] intersects at most t parts of the partition of
V(H) into atomic types over A in H.

# Formalization notes

The bound O_{𝒞,r,s}(|A|^k) is spelled out as a · (|A| + 1)^k, with a
chosen together with k and t, after 𝒞, r and s. The set A* is chosen
before the flip H and the vertex v. The atomic types are taken in the
flip H, as in the paper. The parameter bound s is an input of the lemma,

-/

namespace Lax185574.BallTypes

open Lax185574.Graphs Lax185574.MonadicDependence
open Lax185574.AtomicTypes Lax185574.DefinableFlips Lax185574.GraphBalls

/-- **Few types in balls.** Every finite set `A` has a polynomial-size
superset `A*` such that, in every `s`-definable flip `H`, each ball of
radius `r` that avoids `A*` realizes at most `t` atomic types over `A`
in `H`. -/
axiom ball_types (C : GraphClass) (hC : MonadicallyDependent C) (r s : ℕ) :
    ∃ k t a : ℕ, ∀ G ∈ C, ∀ A : Finset (Fin G.n), ∃ Astar ⊇ A,
      Astar.card ≤ a * (A.card + 1) ^ k ∧
      ∀ H : SimpleGraph (Fin G.n), IsDefinableFlip G.toSimpleGraph s H → ∀ v : Fin G.n,
        Disjoint (graphBall H r {v}) (Astar : Set (Fin G.n)) →
          atomicTypeCount H (graphBall H r {v}) (A : Set (Fin G.n)) ≤ t

end Lax185574.BallTypes

statements.signature:
ball_types : ∀ (C : Lax185574.Graphs.GraphClass),
  Lax185574.MonadicDependence.MonadicallyDependent C →
    ∀ (r s : Nat),
      Exists fun k =>
        Exists fun t =>
          Exists fun a =>
            ∀ (G : Lax185574.Graphs.Graph),
              Set.instMembership.mem C G →
                ∀ (A : Finset (Fin G.n)),
                  Exists fun Astar =>
                    And (GE.ge Astar A)
                      (And (instLENat.le Astar.card (instHMul.hMul a (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd A.card 1) k)))
                        (∀ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin G.n)),
                          Lax185574.DefinableFlips.IsDefinableFlip G.toSimpleGraph s H →
                            ∀ (v : Fin G.n),
                              Disjoint (Lax185574.GraphBalls.graphBall H r (Set.instSingletonSet.singleton v))
                                  (Finset.instSetLike.coe Astar) →
                                instLENat.le
                                  (Lax185574.AtomicTypes.atomicTypeCount H
                                    (Lax185574.GraphBalls.graphBall H r (Set.instSingletonSet.singleton v))
                                    (Finset.instSetLike.coe A))
                                  t))

concepts.title: Merge sequences with definable stages from chains
concepts.description:
For every graph G and chain of length ℓ there is a merge sequence
(𝒬₁, R₁), …, (𝒬_ℓ, R_ℓ) with the following properties.

1. For all r ≥ 1, the radius-r width of the merge sequence is bounded by
   k · π_G(k), where k is the radius-(5r+1) width of the given chain.
2. For each i ∈ [ℓ], the relations ≡_{𝒬_i} and R_i are definable in some
   expansion G^i of G with two unary predicates, using two fixed
   first-order formulas φ_≡(x, y) and φ_R(x, y) of quantifier rank at
   most 5.
3. The merge sequence can be computed in time O(ℓ n³), given G and its
   chain.

Here ≡_𝒬 is the equivalence relation on V(G) whose classes are the parts
of the partition 𝒬.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The two formulas come first, since they are fixed: the same formulas
serve every graph, every chain and every stage. Only the expansion G^i
depends on the stage. They are formulas of graphs with two colors, in
the language of `Lax185574.Colorings`, with the free variables x and y
of `Fin 2`. `StagesDefinable` states the second property for given
formulas.

The merge sequence is produced by a function `M` of the graph and the
chain, and the algorithm `A` computes this function, in the sense of
`Lax185574.Algorithms`. The algorithm and the constant `c` of the time
bound O((ℓ+1) · (n+1)³) come first, so the constant is absolute. The
input is the pair (G, S) and the output is the merge sequence, with
partitions encoded as in `Lax185574.Partitions`. The merge sequence has
length ℓ, the length of the chain. A graph has the vertices `Fin n`,
and the notions of merge sequences and chains are applied to its
`SimpleGraph`. The neighborhood complexity π_G is
`VCDimension.neighborhoodComplexity`.

/-!
---
title: Merge sequences with definable stages from chains
type: lemma
---
For every graph G and chain of length ℓ there is a merge sequence
(𝒬₁, R₁), …, (𝒬_ℓ, R_ℓ) with the following properties.

1. For all r ≥ 1, the radius-r width of the merge sequence is bounded by
   k · π_G(k), where k is the radius-(5r+1) width of the given chain.
2. For each i ∈ [ℓ], the relations ≡_{𝒬_i} and R_i are definable in some
   expansion G^i of G with two unary predicates, using two fixed
   first-order formulas φ_≡(x, y) and φ_R(x, y) of quantifier rank at
   most 5.
3. The merge sequence can be computed in time O(ℓ n³), given G and its
   chain.

Here ≡_𝒬 is the equivalence relation on V(G) whose classes are the parts
of the partition 𝒬.

# Formalization notes

The two formulas come first, since they are fixed: the same formulas
serve every graph, every chain and every stage. Only the expansion G^i
depends on the stage. They are formulas of graphs with two colors, in
the language of `Lax185574.Colorings`, with the free variables x and y
of `Fin 2`. `StagesDefinable` states the second property for given
formulas.

The merge sequence is produced by a function `M` of the graph and the
chain, and the algorithm `A` computes this function, in the sense of
`Lax185574.Algorithms`. The algorithm and the constant `c` of the time
bound O((ℓ+1) · (n+1)³) come first, so the constant is absolute. The
input is the pair (G, S) and the output is the merge sequence, with
partitions encoded as in `Lax185574.Partitions`. The merge sequence has
length ℓ, the length of the chain. A graph has the vertices `Fin n`,
and the notions of merge sequences and chains are applied to its
`SimpleGraph`. The neighborhood complexity π_G is
`VCDimension.neighborhoodComplexity`.
-/

/-- The stages of the merge sequence `ms` are definable by the formulas
`φeq` and `φR`: for every stage there are two color sets such that, in
the expansion of `G` by them, `φeq` defines the equivalence relation of
the partition and `φR` defines the relation of the stage. -/
def StagesDefinable (G : SimpleGraph V) (ms : List (Setoid V × SimpleGraph V))
    (φeq φR : (withColors Language.graph 2).Formula (Fin 2)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : t < ms.length), ∃ colors : Fin 2 → Set V, ∀ x : Fin 2 → V,
    (@Formula.Realize _ V (expansion G colors) _ φeq x ↔ ms[t].1 (x 0) (x 1)) ∧
      (@Formula.Realize _ V (expansion G colors) _ φR x ↔ ms[t].2.Adj (x 0) (x 1))

/-- **Merge sequences from chains.** Two fixed formulas of quantifier
rank at most `5` and one algorithm that computes, from a graph and a
chain of length `ℓ`, a merge sequence of length `ℓ` with the following
properties. (1) For every `r ≥ 1`, its radius-`r` width is at most
`k · π_G(k)` for the radius-`(5r+1)` width `k` of the chain. (2) The two
formulas define its stages. (3) The algorithm takes time
`O((ℓ+1) · (n+1)³)`. -/
axiom exists_mergeSequence_of_chain :
    ∃ (φeq φR : (withColors Language.graph 2).Formula (Fin 2)),
      quantifierRank φeq ≤ 5 ∧ quantifierRank φR ≤ 5 ∧
      ∃ (A : Algorithm) (c : ℕ) (M : (G : Graph) → List (Finset (Fin G.n)) →
          List (Setoid (Fin G.n) × SimpleGraph (Fin G.n))),
        ∀ (G : Graph) (S : List (Finset (Fin G.n))), IsChain S →
          IsMergeSequence G.toSimpleGraph (M G S) ∧ (M G S).length = S.length ∧
          (∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r →
            mergeWidth r (M G S) ≤ chainWidth G.toSimpleGraph (5 * r + 1) S *
              neighborhoodComplexity G.toSimpleGraph (chainWidth G.toSimpleGraph (5 * r + 1) S)) ∧
          StagesDefinable G.toSimpleGraph (M G S) φeq φR ∧
          A.Computes c (G, S) (M G S) ((S.length + 1) * (G.n + 1) ^ 3)

end Lax185574.BetterMergeSequences

concepts.title: A four-part flip of a bipartite graph with short edges in both polarities
concepts.description:
Let B = (X, Y, E) be a bipartite graph with bipartite complement B̄, and
pick arbitrary vertices x ∈ X and y ∈ Y. Partition X according to
adjacency to y, that is, X = X₊ ⊎ X₋ with X₊ = N(y) and X₋ = X ∖ N(y),
and similarly Y = Y₊ ⊎ Y₋ according to x. Then there is a bipartite
graph B′ = (X, Y, E′), obtained from B by some {X₊, X₋, Y₊, Y₋}-flip,
satisfying

for all uv ∈ E′,  dist^B(u, v) ≤ 5  and  dist^{B̄}(u, v) ≤ 5.

This is Lemma A.3 of Drabik, Dumas, Geniet, Nowakowski, Pilipczuk and
Toruńczyk, *Variants of merge-width and applications* (2026).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The parts X and Y are types, and the bipartite graphs B and B̄ are
`bipartiteGraph E` and `bipartiteGraph` of the negated relation, from
`Lax185574.BipartiteGraphs`. Distances are measured by walks from the
copy of u in X to the copy of v in Y.

B′ is again bipartite with parts X and Y, so the flip changes adjacency
only between X and Y, and it is given by its edge relation E′. That B′
is obtained by a {X₊, X₋, Y₊, Y₋}-flip says that for each of the four
pairs of a part of X and a part of Y, either E′ agrees with E on all of
its pairs, or with the negation of E on all of them. The statement
expresses this as: whether E′ agrees with E on a pair uv depends only on
whether u ∈ X₊ and whether v ∈ Y₊.

The cited lemma bounds the distances by 6, and the paper states 5,
noting that the two statements are equivalent. Every walk in a
bipartite graph between a vertex of X and a vertex of Y has odd
length, so a distance at most 6 is at most 5. The statement uses the
bound 5 of the paper.

/-- **Four-part flip of a bipartite graph.** For representatives `x`
and `y`, some flip of `E` on the four parts given by adjacency to `y`
and to `x` keeps only edges `uv` with `dist^B(u, v) ≤ 5` and
`dist^{B̄}(u, v) ≤ 5`. -/
axiom exists_flip_close {X : Type u} {Y : Type w} (E : X → Y → Prop) (x : X) (y : Y) :
    ∃ E' : X → Y → Prop,
      (∀ (u u' : X) (v v' : Y), (E u y ↔ E u' y) → (E x v ↔ E x v') →
        ((E' u v ↔ E u v) ↔ (E' u' v' ↔ E u' v'))) ∧
      ∀ (u : X) (v : Y), E' u v →
        WithinDist (bipartiteGraph E) 5 (.inl u) (.inr v) ∧
          WithinDist (bipartiteGraph fun a b => ¬ E a b) 5 (.inl u) (.inr v)

concepts.title: Bipartite graphs and bipartite complements
concepts.description:
A *bipartite graph* B = (X, Y, E) has parts X and Y and an edge set E
of pairs xy with x ∈ X and y ∈ Y. Its *bipartite complement*, denoted
B̄, is the bipartite graph with parts X, Y and edge set XY ∖ E.

For a graph G and disjoint vertex sets X, Y ⊆ V(G), G[X, Y] is the
bipartite graph with parts X and Y whose edges connect pairs of vertices
that are adjacent in G. Furthermore, G[X, X] denotes the bipartite
graph whose parts are two copies of X, and whose edges connect two
vertices in opposite parts if the corresponding vertices of G are
either adjacent or equal. The edges of G[X, X] connecting the two copies
of a vertex are its *diagonal edges*. Finally, Ḡ[X, X] is the bipartite
complement of G[X, X], extended with the diagonal edges.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A bipartite graph with parts α and β is given by a relation
E : α → β → Prop, and `bipartiteGraph E` is the simple graph on α ⊕ β
that it defines. The bipartite complement is `bipartiteGraph` of the
negated relation.

The graphs G[X, Y] and Ḡ[X, Y] are built uniformly on two copies of the
vertex set, V ⊕ V, as `pairGraph` and `coPairGraph`. The left copy of
X is one part and the right copy of Y is the other. A left vertex u ∈ X
and a right vertex v ∈ Y are adjacent if u = v or u and v are adjacent
in G, respectively non-adjacent in G. For X = Y this is G[X, X], with
its diagonal edges, and Ḡ[X, X]. For disjoint X and Y the case u = v
never occurs, so this is G[X, Y], and Ḡ[X, Y] is its bipartite
complement, the bipartite graph of the non-adjacent pairs. The other
vertices of V ⊕ V are isolated. So the distance from the left copy of u
to the right copy of v in `pairGraph G X Y` is the distance between u
and v in G[X, Y], and likewise for Ḡ[X, Y].

import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic

/-!

title: Bipartite graphs and bipartite complements
type: definition
---

that are adjacent in G. Furthermore, G[X, X] denotes the bipartite
graph whose parts are two copies of X, and whose edges connect two
vertices in opposite parts if the corresponding vertices of G are
either adjacent or equal. The edges of G[X, X] connecting the two copies
of a vertex are its *diagonal edges*. Finally, Ḡ[X, X] is the bipartite
complement of G[X, X], extended with the diagonal edges.

# Formalization notes

that it defines. The bipartite complement is `bipartiteGraph` of the

-/

namespace Lax185574.BipartiteGraphs

universe u w z

/-- The bipartite graph on `α ⊕ β` with an edge between `inl a` and
`inr b` exactly when `E a b`. -/
def bipartiteGraph {α : Type u} {β : Type w} (E : α → β → Prop) : SimpleGraph (α ⊕ β) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun s t => ∃ a b, s = .inl a ∧ t = .inr b ∧ E a b

variable {V : Type z}

/-- `G[X, Y]`, on two copies of `V`: the left copy of `u ∈ X` and the
right copy of `v ∈ Y` are adjacent if `u = v` or `u` and `v` are
adjacent in `G`. -/
def pairGraph (G : SimpleGraph V) (X Y : Set V) : SimpleGraph (V ⊕ V) :=
  bipartiteGraph fun u v => u ∈ X ∧ v ∈ Y ∧ (u = v ∨ G.Adj u v)

/-- `Ḡ[X, Y]`, on two copies of `V`: the left copy of `u ∈ X` and the
right copy of `v ∈ Y` are adjacent if `u = v` or `u` and `v` are
non-adjacent in `G`. -/
def coPairGraph (G : SimpleGraph V) (X Y : Set V) : SimpleGraph (V ⊕ V) :=
  bipartiteGraph fun u v => u ∈ X ∧ v ∈ Y ∧ (u = v ∨ ¬ G.Adj u v)

end Lax185574.BipartiteGraphs

concepts.title: Homogeneous rectangles for colorings of pairs of tuples
concepts.description:
For a tuple ā = (a₁, …, a_ℓ) ∈ [n]^ℓ, the *order type* otp(ā) of ā is
the atomic type of ā in the ordered set ([n], ≤). It stores, for each
i, j ∈ [ℓ], whether aᵢ < aⱼ, aᵢ = aⱼ or aᵢ > aⱼ.

For every k, ℓ ∈ ℕ there is an unbounded, non-decreasing function
U_{k,ℓ} : ℕ → ℕ with the following property. For every t ∈ ℕ and
coloring

c : [t]^ℓ × [t]^ℓ → [k]

there are subsets I, J ⊆ [t] of size U_{k,ℓ}(t) such that c(ā, b̄) only
depends on otp(ā) and otp(b̄), for all ā ∈ I^ℓ and b̄ ∈ J^ℓ.

This is a version of Ramsey's theorem, see Lemma 4.4 of the cited work
on flip-breakability.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The set [t] is `Fin t`, with the same order, and the colors [k] are
`Fin k`. The order type of a tuple records `compare` for every pair of
positions. "c(ā, b̄) only depends on otp(ā) and otp(b̄)" says that any
two pairs of tuples from I^ℓ × J^ℓ with the same order types get the
same color. Unboundedness says that every value is reached. The sets
I and J have exactly U_{k,ℓ}(t) elements.

/-!
---
title: Homogeneous rectangles for colorings of pairs of tuples
type: lemma
---
For a tuple ā = (a₁, …, a_ℓ) ∈ [n]^ℓ, the *order type* otp(ā) of ā is
the atomic type of ā in the ordered set ([n], ≤). It stores, for each

For every k, ℓ ∈ ℕ there is an unbounded, non-decreasing function
U_{k,ℓ} : ℕ → ℕ with the following property. For every t ∈ ℕ and
coloring

c : [t]^ℓ × [t]^ℓ → [k]

there are subsets I, J ⊆ [t] of size U_{k,ℓ}(t) such that c(ā, b̄) only
depends on otp(ā) and otp(b̄), for all ā ∈ I^ℓ and b̄ ∈ J^ℓ.

This is a version of Ramsey's theorem, see Lemma 4.4 of the cited work
on flip-breakability.

# Formalization notes

The set [t] is `Fin t`, with the same order, and the colors [k] are

-/

namespace Lax185574.BipartiteHomogeneity

/-- The order type `otp(ā)` of a tuple of elements of `[t]`: the
comparison of every pair of its entries. -/
def orderType {ℓ t : ℕ} (a : Fin ℓ → Fin t) : Fin ℓ → Fin ℓ → Ordering :=
  fun i j => compare (a i) (a j)

/-- **Homogeneous rectangles.** Every coloring of pairs of
`ℓ`-tuples from `[t]` with `k` colors is determined by the order types
on `I^ℓ × J^ℓ`, for some sets `I` and `J` of size `U_{k,ℓ}(t)`, where
`U_{k,ℓ}` is unbounded and non-decreasing. -/
axiom exists_orderType_homogeneous (k ℓ : ℕ) :
    ∃ U : ℕ → ℕ, Monotone U ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, ∃ t : ℕ, m ≤ U t) ∧
      ∀ (t : ℕ) (c : (Fin ℓ → Fin t) → (Fin ℓ → Fin t) → Fin k),
        ∃ I J : Finset (Fin t), I.card = U t ∧ J.card = U t ∧
          ∀ a a' b b' : Fin ℓ → Fin t,
            (∀ i, a i ∈ I) → (∀ i, a' i ∈ I) → (∀ i, b i ∈ J) → (∀ i, b' i ∈ J) →
            orderType a = orderType a' → orderType b = orderType b' →
            c a b = c a' b'

end Lax185574.BipartiteHomogeneity

exists_orderType_homogeneous : ∀ (k ℓ : Nat),
  Exists fun U =>
    And (Monotone U)
      (And (∀ (m : Nat), Exists fun t => instLENat.le m (U t))
        (∀ (t : Nat) (c : (Fin ℓ → Fin t) → (Fin ℓ → Fin t) → Fin k),
          Exists fun I =>
            Exists fun J =>
              And (Eq I.card (U t))
                (And (Eq J.card (U t))
                  (∀ (a a' b b' : Fin ℓ → Fin t),
                    (∀ (i : Fin ℓ), SetLike.instMembership.mem I (a i)) →
                      (∀ (i : Fin ℓ), SetLike.instMembership.mem I (a' i)) →
                        (∀ (i : Fin ℓ), SetLike.instMembership.mem J (b i)) →
                          (∀ (i : Fin ℓ), SetLike.instMembership.mem J (b' i)) →
                            Eq (Lax185574.BipartiteHomogeneity.orderType a)
                                (Lax185574.BipartiteHomogeneity.orderType a') →
                              Eq (Lax185574.BipartiteHomogeneity.orderType b)
                                  (Lax185574.BipartiteHomogeneity.orderType b') →
                                Eq (c a b) (c a' b')))))

concepts.title: Bounded VC-dimension of monadically dependent classes
concepts.description:
For every monadically dependent graph class 𝒞 there is some d ∈ ℕ such
that every graph G ∈ 𝒞 has VC-dimension at most d.

The paper notes that this is easy to see from the definition of monadic
dependence, and refers to the companion paper for a proof.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The VC-dimension is that of `Lax185574.VCDimension`, an extended natural
number, and "VC-dimension at most d" is `vcDim G.toSimpleGraph ≤ d`. The
paper allows infinite graphs in this part. Here the graphs are those of
a `GraphClass`, which are finite, as in every use.

The constant d is chosen after 𝒞 and before the graph. Monadic
dependence is that of `Lax185574.MonadicDependence`, by transductions.
By `Lax185574.IndependenceProperty` no formula has the independence
property on a monadically dependent class, from which the observation
is immediate: a class whose graphs have unbounded VC-dimension gives the
edge formula the independence property.

concepts.title: Canonical form
concepts.description:
A type tree given by a representation whose sets need not be sorted or
duplicate-free can be brought into canonical form in polynomial time.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The statement is made for one set: a list of elements of an encoded
type, possibly unsorted and with repetitions, is turned into the finite
set of its entries, whose encoding is the sorted duplicate-free list of
the encodings of the elements. The algorithm receives the list of the
encodings of the elements, so every element is preceded by its length,
and it can find the boundaries of the elements without knowing their
type. One algorithm works for all types. A type tree is brought into
canonical form by applying this at every node, from the leaves up. That
step is part of the proofs that use it.

The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`.
Polynomial time means time `O((N + 1)^a)` on an input of length `N`.
The finite set `l.toFinset` needs decidable equality of the elements,
which every type has classically.

concepts.title: Locally definable construction sequences from chains
concepts.description:
For every n-vertex graph G and its chain of length ℓ there is a
construction sequence G₁, …, G_λ of G such that the following properties
hold for all r ≥ 1. Let k_r denote the radius-(5r+1) width of the chain
and w_r ≔ k_r · π_G(k_r).

1. The resulting construction sequence has radius-r width at most w_r
   and length λ ≤ O(n w₁).
2. For every t ∈ [λ−1] and v ∈ V(G), the induced partial graph
   G_t[Ball^{G_{t+1}}_r(v)] is definable in some expansion of G with
   2ℓ+1 unary predicates, using formulas of quantifier rank 7 with w_r
   parameters.
3. The construction sequence can be computed in time O(ℓ n³), given G
   and its chain.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The construction sequence is produced by a function `script` of the
graph and the chain, as a script of `Lax185574.ConstructionSequences`,
and the algorithm `A` computes this function, in the sense of
`Lax185574.Algorithms`. The algorithm, the constant `c` of the time
bound O((ℓ+1) · (n+1)³) and the constant `K` of the length bound come
first, so both constants are absolute. The input is the pair (G, S),
with the encodings of `Lax185574.Encodings`. A graph has the vertices
`Fin n`, and the notions of chains and construction sequences are
applied to its `SimpleGraph`.

The width of item 1 is the radius-r width of
`Lax185574.ConstructionWidth`, which counts parts. The length bound
O(n w₁) is spelled out as K · (n+1) · (w₁+1). The number w_r is
`chainBound G S r`, with π_G the neighborhood complexity
`VCDimension.neighborhoodComplexity`. Item 2 is
`LocalDefinability.IsRadiusDefinable` with 2ℓ+1 predicates, w_r
parameters and rank 7.

Every number in the encoding of the script is at most the length of the
encoding plus n (`Script.HasSmallNumbers`). The paper does not say
this. An algorithm can ensure it by giving the vertices of the initial
partial graph the colors 0, …, n − 1. The bound is what
`Lax185574.DefinableSequences` asks of its output.

import Lax185574.Algorithms

/-!
---
title: Locally definable construction sequences from chains
type: lemma
---
For every n-vertex graph G and its chain of length ℓ there is a
construction sequence G₁, …, G_λ of G such that the following properties
hold for all r ≥ 1. Let k_r denote the radius-(5r+1) width of the chain

   parameters.

graph and the chain, as a script of `Lax185574.ConstructionSequences`,
and the algorithm `A` computes this function, in the sense of
`Lax185574.Algorithms`. The algorithm, the constant `c` of the time
bound O((ℓ+1) · (n+1)³) and the constant `K` of the length bound come
first, so both constants are absolute. The input is the pair (G, S),

namespace Lax185574.ChainConstructionSequences

open Lax185574.Graphs Lax185574.Algorithms
open Lax185574.Chains Lax185574.VCDimension
open Lax185574.ConstructionSequences Lax185574.ConstructionWidth
open Lax185574.LocalDefinability

universe z

/-- The number `w_r = k_r · π_G(k_r)`, where `k_r` is the
radius-`(5r+1)` width of the chain `S`. -/
noncomputable def chainBound {V : Type z} (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : List (Finset V)) (r : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  chainWidth G (5 * r + 1) S * neighborhoodComplexity G (chainWidth G (5 * r + 1) S)

/-- **Construction sequences from chains.** One algorithm computes, from
a graph and a chain of length `ℓ`, a construction sequence of the graph,
given by its script, in time `O((ℓ+1) · (n+1)³)`. For every `r ≥ 1`, it
has radius-`r` width at most `w_r` and length at most
`K · (n+1) · (w₁+1)`, and it is radius-`r` definable with `2ℓ+1`
predicates, `w_r` parameters and rank `7`. -/
axiom exists_constructionSequence_of_chain :
    ∃ (A : Algorithm) (c K : ℕ) (script : (G : Graph) → List (Finset (Fin G.n)) → Script G.n),
      ∀ (G : Graph) (S : List (Finset (Fin G.n))), IsChain S →
        let σ := script G S
        IsConstructionSequence G.toSimpleGraph σ.run ∧ σ.HasSmallNumbers ∧
        σ.run.length ≤ K * (G.n + 1) * (chainBound G.toSimpleGraph S 1 + 1) ∧
        (∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r →
          constructionWidth r σ.run ≤ chainBound G.toSimpleGraph S r ∧
          IsRadiusDefinable G.toSimpleGraph σ.run r (2 * S.length + 1)
            (chainBound G.toSimpleGraph S r) 7) ∧
        A.Computes c (G, S) σ ((S.length + 1) * (G.n + 1) ^ 3)

end Lax185574.ChainConstructionSequences

  Exists fun c =>
    Exists fun K =>
      Exists fun script =>
        ∀ (G : Lax185574.Graphs.Graph) (S : List (Finset (Fin G.n))),
          Lax185574.Chains.IsChain S →
            let σ := script G S;
            And (Lax185574.ConstructionSequences.IsConstructionSequence G.toSimpleGraph σ.run)
              (And σ.HasSmallNumbers
                (And
                  (instLENat.le σ.run.length
                    (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul K (instHAdd.hAdd G.n 1))
                      (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax185574.ChainConstructionSequences.chainBound G.toSimpleGraph S 1) 1)))
                  (And
                    (∀ (r : Nat),
                      instLENat.le 1 r →
                        And
                          (instLENat.le (Lax185574.ConstructionWidth.constructionWidth r σ.run)
                            (Lax185574.ChainConstructionSequences.chainBound G.toSimpleGraph S r))
                          (Lax185574.LocalDefinability.IsRadiusDefinable G.toSimpleGraph σ.run r
                            (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 2 S.length) 1)
                            (Lax185574.ChainConstructionSequences.chainBound G.toSimpleGraph S r) 7))
                    (A.Computes c { fst := G, snd := S } σ
                      (instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd S.length.cast 1) (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd G.n.cast 1) 3))))))

concepts.title: Chains and their radius-r width
concepts.description:
A *chain* in a graph G is a decreasing sequence
V(G) = S₁ ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ S_ℓ = ∅ of vertex sets. Its *radius-r width*, for
r ∈ ℕ, is

max_{2 ≤ i ≤ ℓ} max_{v ∈ V(G)} |ATypes^G(Ball_r^{S_i}(v)/S_{i−1})|
  = max_{2 ≤ i ≤ ℓ} max_{v ∈ V(G)} |Ball_r^{S_i}(v)/𝒫_{S_{i−1}}|,

where Ball_r^S(v) is the ball in the metric of S-flips and 𝒫_S is the
partition into atomic types over S.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The formalization lists a chain in the reverse order, as the increasing
sequence ∅ = S₁ ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ S_ℓ = V(G). A chain is a nonempty list of finite
vertex sets, the first empty, the last the whole vertex set, and each
contained in the next. Consecutive sets may be equal. Reversing the list
turns a chain of the paper into one of the formalization, and the
widths agree after the reversal. A term of the paper pairs a set with
its predecessor, which is the larger set: the ball is taken in the
metric of flips of the smaller set, and the partition into atomic types
over the larger one. In the formalization the term for consecutive sets
S_t ⊆ S_{t+1} takes the ball in the metric of S_t-flips and the
partition 𝒫_{S_{t+1}}, which is the same term.

The width is the second form of the paper: the number of parts of
the partition into atomic types that meet the ball. The vertices of the
ball with the same atomic type over a set S are exactly those in the
same part of 𝒫_S, so the two forms agree. The maximum is the supremum of a set of natural numbers,
finite on a finite vertex type. The empty maximum, for a chain of length
one, is 0.

The chain is the same object for every graph on the vertex set. The
graph enters only the width.

import Lax185574.Flips
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Chains and their radius-r width
type: definition
---

r ∈ ℕ, is

where Ball_r^S(v) is the ball in the metric of S-flips and 𝒫_S is the
partition into atomic types over S.

# Formalization notes

The formalization lists a chain in the reverse order, as the increasing

vertex sets, the first empty, the last the whole vertex set, and each
contained in the next. Consecutive sets may be equal. Reversing the list
turns a chain of the paper into one of the formalization, and the
widths agree after the reversal. A term of the paper pairs a set with
its predecessor, which is the larger set: the ball is taken in the

S_t ⊆ S_{t+1} takes the ball in the metric of S_t-flips and the
partition 𝒫_{S_{t+1}}, which is the same term.

The width is the second form of the paper: the number of parts of
the partition into atomic types that meet the ball. The vertices of the

graph enters only the width.
-/

namespace Lax185574.Chains

open Lax185574.Partitions Lax185574.Flips

universe z

variable {V : Type z}

/-- `S` is a chain: `∅ = S₁ ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ S_m = V`. -/
def IsChain [Fintype V] (S : List (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : S ≠ [], S.head h = ∅ ∧ S.getLast h = Finset.univ ∧
    ∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : t + 1 < S.length), S[t] ⊆ S[t + 1]

/-- The radius-`r` width of the chain `S` in `G`: the largest number of
parts of `𝒫_{S_{t+1}}` that meet a radius-`r` ball in the metric of
`S_t`-flips. -/
noncomputable def chainWidth (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ) (S : List (Finset V)) : ℕ :=
  sSup {K | ∃ (t : ℕ) (ht : t + 1 < S.length) (v : V),
    K = partCount (atomicTypes G (S[t + 1] : Set V))
      (flipBall G (atomicTypes G (S[t] : Set V)) r v)}

end Lax185574.Chains

concepts.title: Chains of vertex sets with few atomic types in flip-metric balls
concepts.description:
Let r ∈ ℕ and 𝒞 be a monadically dependent graph class. Then for any
rational ε > 0 and an n-vertex graph G ∈ 𝒞, there is a sequence of
vertex subsets

∅ = B_m ⊆ B_{m−1} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ B₁ ⊆ B₀ = V(G)

with m ≤ O(r/ε) that satisfies the following condition: for every
i ∈ [m] and u ∈ V(G), Ball^r_{𝒯₁(G,B_i)}[u] intersects at most
O_{𝒞,r,ε}(n^ε) parts of 𝒯₁(G, B_{i−1}). Moreover, given ε, r and G, such
a sequence B₀, B₁, …, B_m can be computed in Õ_{𝒞,r}(n³) time.

This is Theorem 4.4 of Dreier, Mählmann, Pilipczuk and Toruńczyk,
*Monadically dependent graph classes have almost bounded merge-width*
(2026), the companion paper. Here 𝒯₁(G, B) is the
partition of V(G) into 1-types over B, that is, into atomic types, and Ball^r_𝒫[u] is the radius-r ball of the
𝒫-flip metric.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
In the companion paper ℕ is the set of positive integers, so r ≥ 1. Its
1-types over B are the atomic types over B, `Partitions.atomicTypes`,
and its flips and flip-metric balls are those of `Lax185574.Flips`,
with distances measured by shortest paths. A sequence B₀, …, B_m is the
list [B₀, …, B_m], in the order of the companion paper, which is the
reverse of the order of chains in `Lax185574.Chains`. The bound m ≤
O(r/ε) on the number of steps becomes a bound K · r/ε + K on the length
m + 1 of the list.

The algorithm `A` is chosen before the class, and the sequence is a
function `chain` of r, ε and the graph that `A` computes, in the sense
of `Lax185574.Algorithms`. The companion paper notes that the algorithm
of its Damping Theorem does not depend on the class, and the algorithm
of this theorem iterates it. The bound on the length in its proof uses only the Damping Theorem for
the graph at hand, which holds for every graph with that graph's own
constants (every graph lies in the monadically dependent class {G}).
The proof gives m ≤ 1 + 2r/ε on every graph with at least two vertices,
and graphs with at most one vertex are handled directly. So the length
bound is stated for every graph. The input is the triple (r, ε, G) and
the output is the list of sets.

The time bound Õ_{𝒞,r}(n³) hides a subpolynomial factor that depends on
𝒞 and r. It is spelled out as O(n^{3+δ}) for every real δ > 0, with a
constant c chosen after 𝒞, r, ε and δ. In the companion paper the time
bound does not depend on ε, so this is weaker. The width bound is
c · (n+1)^ε with the same constant.

The algorithm of the companion paper uses integers of n^{o(1)} bits.
Stored in several words, they cost a subpolynomial factor, which the
bound O(n^{3+δ}) absorbs, so the word lengths are those of
`Lax185574.Algorithms`, with the word-length exponent of the algorithm,
which is chosen before the class.

namespace Lax185574.ChainTheorem

open Lax185574.Graphs Lax185574.MonadicDependence Lax185574.Algorithms
open Lax185574.Partitions Lax185574.Flips

universe z

variable {V : Type z}

/-- `B` is a decreasing sequence of vertex sets `V = B₀ ⊇ B₁ ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ B_m = ∅`. -/
def IsDecreasingChain [Fintype V] (B : List (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : B ≠ [], B.head h = Finset.univ ∧ B.getLast h = ∅ ∧
    ∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : t + 1 < B.length), B[t + 1] ⊆ B[t]

/-- For every `i ∈ [m]` and vertex `u`, the radius-`r` ball around `u`
in the metric of `B_i`-flips meets at most `K` parts of the partition
into atomic types over `B_{i−1}`. -/
def BallsMeetFewTypes (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ) (K : ℝ) (B : List (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : t + 1 < B.length) (u : V),
    (partCount (atomicTypes G (B[t] : Set V))
      (flipBall G (atomicTypes G (B[t + 1] : Set V)) r u) : ℝ) ≤ K

/-- **Chain theorem of the companion paper.** One algorithm computes,
from `r ≥ 1`, a rational `ε > 0` and a graph, a decreasing sequence
`V = B₀ ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ B_m = ∅` of length at most `K · r/ε + K`. On members of a
monadically dependent class, every radius-`r` ball of the `B_i`-flip
metric meets at most `c · (n+1)^ε` atomic types over `B_{i−1}`, and the

from `r ≥ 1`, a rational `ε > 0` and a graph, a decreasing sequence

concepts.title: Closure theorem
concepts.description:
For every monadically dependent graph class 𝒞 and radius r ∈ ℕ there are
some c, s ∈ ℕ with the following property.

For every G ∈ 𝒞 and finite set A ⊆ V(G) there is a set A* ⊆ V(G) of size
O_{𝒞,r}(|A|^c) such that for every vertex v ∉ A there is a set
S(v) ⊆ A* of size at most s and an S(v)-definable flip H with

dist^H(v, A) > r.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The bound O_{𝒞,r}(|A|^c) is spelled out as a · (|A| + 1)^c, with a
chosen together with c and s, after 𝒞 and r. Since c is existentially
quantified, this is equivalent to the paper's a·|A|^c + b. An
S(v)-definable flip is an S(v)-flip, that is a flip for the partition
`Partitions.atomicTypes` of G into atomic types over S(v). These are
the flips G ⊕ (p̄, R) for the tuples p̄ listing S(v). The condition
dist^H(v, A) > r is stated as Ball^H_r[v] ∩ A = ∅.

The set A* need not contain A, as in the paper. The paper proves the
theorem for finite or infinite graphs. Here 𝒞 is a `GraphClass`, so its
members are finite, which is the case used in the model-checking
theorem. Monadic dependence is that of `Lax185574.MonadicDependence`,
by transductions, as in the paper.

such that each vertex outside `A` is separated from `A` at distance more
than `r` by a flip over at most `s` vertices of `A*`. -/
axiom closure_theorem (C : GraphClass) (hC : MonadicallyDependent C) (r : ℕ) :
    ∃ c s a : ℕ, ∀ G ∈ C, ∀ A : Finset (Fin G.n), ∃ Astar : Finset (Fin G.n),

end Lax185574.ClosureTheorem

concepts.title: Closure theorem for tuples
concepts.description:
For every monadically dependent graph class 𝒞, radius r ∈ ℕ, and tuple
size k ∈ ℕ, there are some c, s ∈ ℕ with the following property.

For every G ∈ 𝒞 and finite set A ⊆ V(G) there is a set ℋ of
O_{𝒞,r,k}(|A|^c) many s-flips of G such that for every tuple
v̄ ∈ (V(G) ∖ A)^k there is a flip H ∈ ℋ with

dist^H(v̄, A) > r.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The bound O_{𝒞,r,k}(|A|^c) is spelled out as a · (|A| + 1)^c, with a
chosen together with c and s, after 𝒞, r and k. The set ℋ is a finite
set of graphs on the vertex set of G, each an s-flip, that is a 𝒫-flip
for a partition 𝒫 into at most s parts. The number of parts is the
cardinality of the quotient, which is finite as the graph is finite.
The flips need not be definable. The condition dist^H(v̄, A) > r, for
the minimum distance between the entries of v̄ and A, is stated as
disjointness of A from the ball of radius r around the entries of v̄.
The graphs of 𝒞 are finite, as in `ClosureTheorem`.

    (r k : ℕ) :

concepts.title: Clustering of a tuple
concepts.description:
Let r ∈ ℕ, ℓ ≥ 1, G a graph and ā = (a₁, …, a_ℓ) ∈ V(G)^ℓ. There exist a
radius ρ with r ≤ ρ ≤ 9^{ℓ−1} r and a partition 𝓑 of {a₁, …, a_ℓ} with
the following property. For every X ⊆ V(G), every inclusion-wise
maximal 4ρ-scattered subset S ⊆ X, and every H ≥ 4ρ + r,

  ∃x ∈ X: dist(x, ā) > r
  ⟺ ∃x ∈ X: r < dist(x, ā) ≤ H,
     or |{B ∈ 𝓑 | ∃x ∈ X: dist(x, B) ≤ r}| < |S|.

Moreover, ρ and 𝓑 can be determined by tests of the form
dist(aᵢ, aⱼ) ≤ s, where i, j ∈ [ℓ] and s ≤ 8 · 9^{ℓ−1} r.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The paper cites Corollary 3.4 and Lemma 3.5 of its locality note. The
statement here makes "can be determined by tests" explicit by naming a
criterion that the tests decide. A radius ρ and a partition are
*admissible* if entries in the same block are within distance 4ρ − 2r
of each other, and entries in different blocks are not within distance
4ρ + 2r. The statement says that an admissible pair with
r ≤ ρ ≤ 9^{ℓ−1} r exists, and that every admissible pair with r ≤ ρ has
the property above. Admissibility of a pair involves only tests
dist(aᵢ, aⱼ) ≤ s with s ≤ 4 · 9^{ℓ−1} r + 2r ≤ 8 · 9^{ℓ−1} r. So an
algorithm that knows these tests finds a suitable pair by trying all
candidates. A statement that only asserts that the pair is some
function of the tests would not let an algorithm compute it.

The graph is finite. The partition is given on the positions: a function
β : [ℓ] → [ℓ] puts the positions i and j in the same block when
β(i) = β(j). dist(x, ā) > r means that x is within distance r of no
entry, and r < dist(x, ā) ≤ H means that x is within distance r of no
entry and within distance H of some entry.

import Lax185574.GaifmanGraph
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card

/-!
---
title: Clustering of a tuple
type: lemma
---
Let r ∈ ℕ, ℓ ≥ 1, G a graph and ā = (a₁, …, a_ℓ) ∈ V(G)^ℓ. There exist a

maximal 4ρ-scattered subset S ⊆ X, and every H ≥ 4ρ + r,

  ∃x ∈ X: dist(x, ā) > r
  ⟺ ∃x ∈ X: r < dist(x, ā) ≤ H,
     or |{B ∈ 𝓑 | ∃x ∈ X: dist(x, B) ≤ r}| < |S|.

Moreover, ρ and 𝓑 can be determined by tests of the form

# Formalization notes

statement here makes "can be determined by tests" explicit by naming a

*admissible* if entries in the same block are within distance 4ρ − 2r

-/

namespace Lax185574.Clustering

open Lax185574.GaifmanGraph

variable {V : Type*}

/-- The radius `ρ` and the partition `β` of the positions are
admissible for `a` at radius `r`: entries in one block are within
distance `4ρ − 2r`, and entries in different blocks are not within
distance `4ρ + 2r`. -/
def Admissible (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ) {ℓ : ℕ} (a : Fin ℓ → V) (ρ : ℕ)
    (β : Fin ℓ → Fin ℓ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, (β i = β j → WithinDist G (4 * ρ - 2 * r) (a i) (a j)) ∧
    (β i ≠ β j → ¬ WithinDist G (4 * ρ + 2 * r) (a i) (a j))

/-- **Clustering.** Some admissible radius lies between `r` and
`9^(ℓ−1) r`, and every admissible pair detects the vertices of a set `X`
far from `a`: by vertices at bounded distance, or by counting a maximal
scattered subset of `X`. -/
axiom clustering [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (r ℓ : ℕ) (hℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ) (a : Fin ℓ → V) :
    (∃ ρ β, r ≤ ρ ∧ ρ ≤ 9 ^ (ℓ - 1) * r ∧ Admissible G r a ρ β) ∧
    ∀ ρ β, r ≤ ρ → Admissible G r a ρ β →
      ∀ (X S : Set V) (H : ℕ), S ⊆ X →
        (∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x ≠ y → ¬ WithinDist G (4 * ρ) x y) →
        (∀ x ∈ X, ∃ y ∈ S, WithinDist G (4 * ρ) x y) →
        4 * ρ + r ≤ H →
        ((∃ x ∈ X, ∀ i, ¬ WithinDist G r (a i) x) ↔
          (∃ x ∈ X, (∀ i, ¬ WithinDist G r (a i) x) ∧ ∃ i, WithinDist G H (a i) x) ∨
          (β '' {i | ∃ x ∈ X, WithinDist G r (a i) x}).ncard < S.ncard)

end Lax185574.Clustering

concepts.title: Colorings of graphs
concepts.description:
A *coloring* of a graph G is an expansion G⁺ of G by finitely many unary
predicates. With c predicates, G⁺ is a structure in the signature of
graphs expanded by c unary symbols.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The colored language and the color sets are those of
`Lax710763.Transductions`, which the archive's monadic dependence is
stated over. The c color sets are arbitrary: they may overlap and need
not cover the vertex set. The expansion is the structure of the sum
language, which interprets adjacency by `G` and the i-th color by the
i-th color set.

The main theorem, monadic dependence and the independence property use
the formulas of `Lax185574.FirstOrderLogic`, with a coloring given by
one set of vertices per color. The statements about types and
definability use the formulas of mathlib in the colored language here,
since mathlib provides the quantifier rank, parameters and the sets of
formulas that types are made of. In both, a coloring with c colors is
a family of c sets of vertices, which may overlap.

import Lax710763.Transductions
import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Graph

/-!
---
title: Colorings of graphs
type: definition
---
A *coloring* of a graph G is an expansion G⁺ of G by finitely many unary
predicates. With c predicates, G⁺ is a structure in the signature of
graphs expanded by c unary symbols.

# Formalization notes

The colored language and the color sets are those of
`Lax710763.Transductions`, which the archive's monadic dependence is
stated over. The c color sets are arbitrary: they may overlap and need
not cover the vertex set. The expansion is the structure of the sum
language, which interprets adjacency by `G` and the i-th color by the
i-th color set.

The main theorem, monadic dependence and the independence property use
the formulas of `Lax185574.FirstOrderLogic`, with a coloring given by
one set of vertices per color. The statements about types and
definability use the formulas of mathlib in the colored language here,
since mathlib provides the quantifier rank, parameters and the sets of
formulas that types are made of. In both, a coloring with c colors is
a family of c sets of vertices, which may overlap.
-/

namespace Lax185574.Colorings

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Lax710763.Transductions

universe z

variable {V : Type z}

/-- The expansion `G⁺` of the graph `G` by the color sets `colors`. -/
@[implicit_reducible]
def expansion (G : SimpleGraph V) {c : ℕ} (colors : Fin c → Set V) :
    (withColors Language.graph c).Structure V :=
  @Language.sumStructure _ _ V G.structure (colorStructure colors)

end Lax185574.Colorings

concepts.title: A graph or its complement has diameter at most 3
concepts.description:
For every graph G, at least one of G and Ḡ has diameter at most 3.

This is folklore.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
"Diameter at most 3" says that any two vertices are joined by a walk of
length at most 3, `WithinDist` of `Lax185574.GaifmanGraph`. The
complement Ḡ is the complement `Gᶜ`, whose edges are the pairs of
distinct non-adjacent vertices. The graph may be infinite.

concepts.title: Computing the scatter type
concepts.description:
There is an algorithm which, given a nonempty partial graph G, numbers
k ≥ 1 and q ∈ ℕ, its distance matrix D_G, and the family
(tree_{k,q}(a) : a ∈ V(G)), computes stp^G_{k,q} in time

  |G|² · poly_{k,q}(max_{a ∈ V(G)} ‖tree_{k,q}(a)‖).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`,
one for all k and q. Its input is the tuple of G, k, q, the distance
matrix and the family of type trees, with the encodings of
`Lax185574.Encodings`. The partial graph is on `Fin n`, so |G| = n, and
it is nonempty when 1 ≤ n. The output is the scatter type, a finite set
as in `Lax185574.ScatterTypes`. The largest size of a tree of the
family is `maxTreeSize G k q`, and the time is
`O(n² · (maxTreeSize G k q + 1)^a)`, where the degree `a` and the
constant `c` may depend on k and q. The second factor is increased by
one, so that it is positive.

concepts.title: Computing chains of small width
concepts.description:
There is an algorithm which, given an n-vertex graph G, a radius r ∈ ℕ
and a rational ε > 0, computes a chain of G of length O(r/ε) and radius-r
width O_{𝒞,r,ε}(n^ε), and runs in time Ô_{𝒞,r}(n³), where 𝒞 is any
monadically dependent graph class containing G. Here Ô_k(n^c) stands for
a bound O_{k,δ}(n^{c+δ}) for every δ > 0.

The paper cites this as Theorem 4.4 of the companion paper
*Monadically dependent graph classes have almost bounded merge-width*
(see `Lax185574.ChainTheorem`).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The radius is at least 1, which is the case used. The chain is
produced by a function `chain` of r, ε and the graph, and the algorithm
`A` computes this function, in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`. The
algorithm and the absolute constant `K` of the length bound come first.
On every graph the output is a chain of length at most K · r/ε + K. The
algorithm does not depend on the class. For a monadically dependent
class 𝒞, a radius r and ε, the constant `c` bounds the width by
c · (n+1)^ε on the members of 𝒞. The input is the triple (r, ε, G) and
the output is the list of the sets of the chain. The chain is listed in
increasing order, ∅ = S₁ ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ S_m = V(G), as in `Lax185574.Chains`.
This is the reverse of the order of the paper.

**Deviation from the paper.** The paper claims the running time
Ô_{𝒞,r}(n³), whose constant does not depend on ε. Here the time bound
is O(n^{3+δ}) on members of 𝒞 for every δ > 0, with a constant c
depending on 𝒞, r, ε and δ, as in `Lax185574.ChainTheorem`. This is
weaker than the paper and is what `Lax185574.DefinableSequences`
needs. A caller chooses δ independently of ε, so that the time fits the
word lengths of its own statement. The statement is the companion
paper's theorem with the chain reversed. The word lengths at which the
statement speaks also depend on the class, through c, as in
`Lax185574.DefinableSequences`.

type: theorem

namespace Lax185574.ComputingChains

open Lax185574.Graphs Lax185574.MonadicDependence Lax185574.Algorithms Lax185574.Chains

/-- **Computing chains.** One algorithm computes, from `r ≥ 1`, a
rational `ε > 0` and a graph, a chain of length at most `K · r/ε + K`. On
members of a monadically dependent class, the chain has radius-`r` width
at most `c · (n+1)^ε`, and for every `δ > 0` the algorithm takes time
`O(n^(3+δ))`, with `c` depending also on `δ`. -/
axiom exists_program_chain :
    ∃ (A : Algorithm) (K : ℕ) (chain : ℕ → ℚ → (G : Graph) → List (Finset (Fin G.n))),
      (∀ (r : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) (G : Graph), 1 ≤ r → 0 < ε →
        IsChain (chain r ε G) ∧ ((chain r ε G).length : ℚ) ≤ K * r / ε + K) ∧
      ∀ C : GraphClass, MonadicallyDependent C → ∀ (r : ℕ) (ε : ℚ), 1 ≤ r → 0 < ε →
        ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ G ∈ C,
          (chainWidth G.toSimpleGraph r (chain r ε G) : ℝ) ≤ c * ((G.n : ℝ) + 1) ^ (ε : ℝ) ∧
          A.Computes c (r, ε, G) (chain r ε G) ((G.n : ℝ) ^ (3 + δ))

end Lax185574.ComputingChains

    Exists fun chain =>

            Rat.instLT.lt 0 ε →
              And (Lax185574.Chains.IsChain (chain r ε G))
                (Rat.instLE.le (chain r ε G).length.cast
                  (instHAdd.hAdd (instHDiv.hDiv (instHMul.hMul K.cast r.cast) ε) K.cast)))
        (∀ (C : Lax185574.Graphs.GraphClass),
          Lax185574.MonadicDependence.MonadicallyDependent C →

                Rat.instLT.lt 0 ε →
                  ∀ (δ : Real),
                    Real.instLT.lt 0 δ →
                      Exists fun c =>
                        ∀ (G : Lax185574.Graphs.Graph),

concepts.title: Model checking along a construction sequence
concepts.description:
There is an algorithm which, given a sentence φ and an n-vertex graph G
together with a construction sequence of G of length λ, determines
whether G ⊨ φ in time

λ · n² · poly_φ(K),

where K is the radius-r depth-d width of the construction sequence, for
some r and d that depend only on φ.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`,
one for all sentences. For each sentence there are the radius `r`, the
depth `d`, the degree `b` and the constant `c` of the time bound. The
input is the triple of G, a script of the construction sequence and φ,
with the encodings of `Lax185574.Encodings`. The construction sequence
is the run of the script, see `Lax185574.ConstructionSequences`, so λ is
the length of the run. K is the width of `Lax185574.Width`.

The time bound λ · n² · poly_φ(K) is spelled out as
`λ · (n+1)² · (K+1)^b`. The graph without vertices has construction
sequences of every length, and the factor (n+1)² keeps the bound large
enough to read them. The paper says that r and d are computable from
φ. Here they only exist. The algorithm is correct on every construction
sequence, whatever its width. So an algorithm that needs r and d can try
all pairs in parallel, and the right pair costs only a constant factor
that depends on φ.

namespace Lax185574.ConstructionModelChecking

open Lax185574.Graphs Lax185574.FirstOrderLogic Lax185574.Algorithms
open Lax185574.ConstructionSequences Lax185574.Width

/-- **Model checking along a construction sequence.** One algorithm
decides `G ⊨ φ`, given `G`, a construction sequence of `G` by its

concepts.title: Construction sequences
concepts.description:
For colors P, Q and a partial graph G, the partial graphs merge_{P,Q}(G)
(for P ≠ Q), resolve⁺_{P,Q}(G) and resolve⁻_{P,Q}(G) are obtained from G
by leaving everything unchanged, apart from the following:

- merge_{P,Q}(G): P^H = P^G ∪ Q^G and Q^H = ∅, for P ≠ Q;
- resolve⁺_{P,Q}(G): E(H) = E(G) ∪ (P^G Q^G ∖ N(G));
- resolve⁻_{P,Q}(G): N(H) = N(G) ∪ (P^G Q^G ∖ E(G)).

Here P^G Q^G is the set of pairs xy of distinct vertices with x ∈ P^G and
y ∈ Q^G. After either resolve, every pair in P^G Q^G is resolved.

An *initial* partial graph has no resolved pairs, and every part is a
singleton. A *construction sequence* of a graph G = (V, E) is a sequence
G₁, …, G_λ of partial graphs with vertex set V such that G₁ is initial,
every step is one merge or one resolve, and G_λ has a single part,
E(G_λ) = E and N(G_λ) = (V choose 2) ∖ E.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A sequence is a nonempty list of partial graphs. Its first entry is G₁,
and the step condition relates consecutive entries `s[t]` and `s[t+1]`.
"Every part is a singleton" says that the coloring is injective, and "a
single part" says that all vertices have the same color. The colors P
and Q of a step are arbitrary natural numbers, as in the paper. A resolve naming a color that no vertex
has, or a merge whose second color no vertex has, changes nothing, and
is still counted as a step. Such steps only lengthen a sequence. The pairs `P^G Q^G` are built with `SimpleGraph.fromRel`,
which symmetrizes the relation and removes the diagonal.

The paper defines construction sequences twice, in the technical
overview through merges and resolves of parts, and in the preliminaries
of the model-checking part through the operators on colors above. Both
passages describe the same sequences. A merge of two distinct parts is a
merge of their colors, and a resolve of two parts is a resolve of their
colors.

Algorithms receive and produce a construction sequence on `Fin n` as a
`Script`: the colors of the initial partial graph, which has no resolved
pairs, and the list of the steps. `Script.run` is the sequence it
produces, the initial partial graph followed by the results of the
steps. The derived encoding of `Lax185574.Encoding` writes a script as
n, the n colors, the number of steps, and then each step as three
numbers, an opcode (0 for a merge, 1 for a positive resolve and 2 for a
negative resolve) followed by the colors P and Q. Nothing in a script
forces its colors to be distinct, or its sequence to be a construction
sequence of a particular graph. Those are properties of the sequence,
stated through `IsConstructionSequence` where they are needed.

/-!

title: Construction sequences
type: definition
---

namespace Lax185574.ConstructionSequences

open Lax185574.PartialGraphs

universe z

variable {V : Type z}

/-- The pairs `P^G Q^G`: distinct vertices, one of color `P` and the
other of color `Q`. -/
def between (G : PartialGraph V) (P Q : ℕ) : SimpleGraph V :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun x y => G.color x = P ∧ G.color y = Q

/-- `merge_{P,Q}(G)`: the vertices of color `Q` get color `P`. -/
def merge (G : PartialGraph V) (P Q : ℕ) : PartialGraph V :=
  { G with color := fun v => if G.color v = Q then P else G.color v }

/-- `resolve⁺_{P,Q}(G)`: the unresolved pairs in `P^G Q^G` become
edges. -/
def resolvePos (G : PartialGraph V) (P Q : ℕ) : PartialGraph V where
  edge := G.edge ⊔ (between G P Q \ G.nonEdge)
  nonEdge := G.nonEdge
  disjoint := disjoint_sup_left.2 ⟨G.disjoint, disjoint_sdiff_self_left⟩
  color := G.color

/-- `resolve⁻_{P,Q}(G)`: the unresolved pairs in `P^G Q^G` become
non-edges. -/
def resolveNeg (G : PartialGraph V) (P Q : ℕ) : PartialGraph V where
  edge := G.edge
  nonEdge := G.nonEdge ⊔ (between G P Q \ G.edge)
  disjoint := disjoint_sup_right.2 ⟨G.disjoint, disjoint_sdiff_self_right⟩
  color := G.color

/-- An initial partial graph: no resolved pairs, and every part is a
singleton. -/
def IsInitial (G : PartialGraph V) : Prop :=
  G.edge = ⊥ ∧ G.nonEdge = ⊥ ∧ Function.Injective G.color

/-- `H` is obtained from `G` by one merge or one resolve. -/
def IsStep (G H : PartialGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ P Q : ℕ, (P ≠ Q ∧ H = merge G P Q) ∨ H = resolvePos G P Q ∨
    H = resolveNeg G P Q

/-- `s` is a construction sequence of the graph `G`: it starts with an
initial partial graph, each entry is obtained from the previous one by
one merge or one resolve, and the last entry has a single part, the
edges of `G` as edges and the non-edges of `G` as non-edges. -/
def IsConstructionSequence (G : SimpleGraph V) (s : List (PartialGraph V)) :
    Prop :=
  ∃ h : s ≠ [],
    IsInitial (s.head h) ∧
    (∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : t + 1 < s.length), IsStep s[t] s[t + 1]) ∧
    (∀ u v : V, (s.getLast h).color u = (s.getLast h).color v) ∧
    (s.getLast h).edge = G ∧ (s.getLast h).nonEdge = Gᶜ

open Lax185574.Encoding

/-- One step of a construction sequence. -/
inductive Step
  /-- `merge_{P,Q}`. -/
  | merge (P Q : ℕ)
  /-- `resolve⁺_{P,Q}`. -/
  | resolvePos (P Q : ℕ)
  /-- `resolve⁻_{P,Q}`. -/
  | resolveNeg (P Q : ℕ)
  deriving Encode

/-- The partial graph obtained by applying a step. -/
def apply (G : PartialGraph V) : Step → PartialGraph V
  | .merge P Q => merge G P Q
  | .resolvePos P Q => resolvePos G P Q
  | .resolveNeg P Q => resolveNeg G P Q

/-- The partial graph with no resolved pairs and the given colors. -/
def unresolved (color : V → ℕ) : PartialGraph V where
  edge := ⊥
  nonEdge := ⊥
  disjoint := disjoint_bot_left
  color := color

/-- A construction script on `Fin n`: the colors of the initial partial
graph, which has no resolved pairs, and the steps. -/
structure Script (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The colors of the initial partial graph. -/
  colors : Fin n → ℕ
  /-- The steps, in order. -/
  steps : List Step
  deriving Encode

/-- The sequence produced by a script: the initial partial graph
followed by the results of the steps. -/
def Script.run {n : ℕ} (σ : Script n) : List (PartialGraph (Fin n)) :=
  σ.steps.scanl apply (unresolved σ.colors)

/-- Every number in the encoding of the script `σ` is at most the
length of the encoding plus `n`. This holds when the colors of the
initial partial graph and of the steps are vertices. It lets an
algorithm pass the script on to another one, whose word length depends
on the numbers of its input. -/
def Script.HasSmallNumbers {n : ℕ} (σ : Script n) : Prop :=
  ∀ v ∈ encode σ, v ≤ (encode σ).length + n

/-- The list `y` encodes the sequence `s` of partial graphs on `n`
vertices: it is the encoding of a script that produces `s`. -/
def EncodesSequence {n : ℕ} (y : List ℕ) (s : List (PartialGraph (Fin n))) :
    Prop :=
  ∃ σ : Script n, y = encode σ ∧ s = σ.run

end Lax185574.ConstructionSequences

concepts.title: Radius-r width of a construction sequence
concepts.description:
Partial graphs, construction sequences and their radius-r width are
defined in the technical overview of the paper. A construction sequence
of a graph G with vertex set V is a sequence G₁, …, G_λ of partial
graphs with vertex set V. Its *radius-r width* is the maximum, over all
t ∈ [λ] and v ∈ V, of the number of parts of G_t that intersect
Ball^{G_t}_r(v). The ball is taken in the Gaifman graph (V, R(G_t)) of
G_t, whose edges are the resolved pairs E(G_t) ∪ N(G_t). The radius-r
merge-width of G is the minimum radius-r width over all construction
sequences of G.

For a partial graph H with partition 𝒫 and a set W ⊆ V(H), the induced
partial graph H[W] has vertex set W, edges E(H) ∩ (W choose 2),
non-edges N(H) ∩ (W choose 2), and partition { P ∩ W : P ∈ 𝒫 } ∖ {∅}.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A construction sequence is a list of partial graphs, as in
`Lax185574.ConstructionSequences`. The Gaifman graph (V, R(G_t)) is the
graph of resolved pairs, so the ball is `PartialGraph.ball`. The
parts of a partial graph are its nonempty color classes, so the parts
meeting a set B correspond to the colors of the vertices of B, and their
number is the number of these colors. The maximum is the supremum of a
set of natural numbers, which is finite when the vertex type is finite.
The empty maximum is 0.

This width counts parts. It is not the radius-r depth-q width of
`Lax185574.Width`, which counts types. The merge-width of a graph is not
needed and is not defined here.

The induced partial graph H[W] is the induced substructure of
`Lax185574.GaifmanGraph` on the structure of H, see
`Lax185574.PartialGraphs`. Its colors are those of H restricted to W, so
its parts are the nonempty sets P ∩ W.

namespace Lax185574.ConstructionWidth

open Lax185574.PartialGraphs

universe z

variable {V : Type z}

/-- The radius-`r` width of the sequence `s`: the largest number of
parts of `s[t]` that meet a ball of radius `r` in the resolved pairs of
`s[t]`. -/
noncomputable def constructionWidth (r : ℕ) (s : List (PartialGraph V)) : ℕ :=
  sSup {K | ∃ (t : ℕ) (ht : t < s.length) (v : V),

end Lax185574.ConstructionWidth

concepts.title: The edges of a definable flip are quantifier-free definable
concepts.description:
The edges of a definable flip can be defined in the original graph. More
precisely, for every s ∈ ℕ and symmetric relation R ⊆ Π^s × Π^s there
exists a quantifier-free formula E_{⊕R}(x, y, z̄) such that for every
graph G, tuple p̄ ∈ V(G)^s, and vertices u, v ∈ V(G),

G ⊕ (p̄, R) ⊨ E(u, v)  ⟺  G ⊨ E_{⊕R}(u, v, p̄).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The formula is in mathlib's language of graphs with the free variables
`Fin 2 ⊕ Fin s`: the left summand is (x, y) and the right summand is z̄.
Quantifier-free is mathlib's `IsQF`. The formula is chosen before the
graph, so one formula works for all graphs on all vertex types of a
fixed universe, finite or infinite. G ⊕ (p̄, R) ⊨ E(u, v) is adjacency
in `DefinableFlips.flipOver`.

# Formalization notes

namespace Lax185574.DefinableFlipFormula

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language
open Lax185574.AtomicTypes Lax185574.DefinableFlips

universe u

/-- **Definable flips are quantifier-free definable.** For a symmetric
relation `R` on atomic types over `s`-tuples, one quantifier-free
formula `E_{⊕R}(x, y, z̄)` defines the edges of `G ⊕ (p̄, R)` in `G`, for
every graph `G` and tuple `p̄`. -/
axiom exists_isQF_flipOver_formula (s : ℕ)
    (R : (Fin s → PairType) → (Fin s → PairType) → Prop)
    (hR : ∀ P Q, R P Q → R Q P) :
    ∃ φ : Language.graph.Formula (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin s), φ.IsQF ∧
      ∀ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : Fin s → V) (x y : V),
        (flipOver G p R).Adj x y ↔
          @Formula.Realize Language.graph V G.structure _ φ (Sum.elim ![x, y] p)

end Lax185574.DefinableFlipFormula

concepts.title: Definable flips
concepts.description:
For s ∈ ℕ, an s-tuple p̄ = (p₁, …, p_s) of vertices of a graph G and a
symmetric relation R ⊆ Π^s × Π^s, the graph G ⊕ (p̄, R) is the
{p₁, …, p_s}-flip H of G obtained by partitioning V(G) into atomic types
over p̄ and then flipping according to R. More precisely, for
uv ∈ (V choose 2),

uv ∈ E(H) △ E(G)  ⟺  (atp^G(u/p̄), atp^G(v/p̄)) ∈ R.

Such a flip is called *s-definable*. Equivalently, an s-definable flip
is an S-flip for some S ⊆ V(G) of size at most s. An s-definable flip is
also s'-definable for every s' ≥ s.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
An S-flip of G is a flip for the partition into atomic types over S,
`Flips.IsFlip G (Partitions.atomicTypes G S) H`.

The graph G ⊕ (p̄, R) is `flipOver G p R`. It is built with
`SimpleGraph.fromRel`, which removes the diagonal and symmetrizes. For a
symmetric relation R the relation that is symmetrized is already
symmetric, so two distinct vertices are adjacent in `flipOver G p R`
exactly when their adjacency in G differs from membership of their
atomic types in R. Every statement about `flipOver` assumes R symmetric.

An s-definable flip, `IsDefinableFlip G s H`, is defined by the second,
equivalent formulation: an S-flip for a finite set S of at most s
vertices. The two formulations agree on every graph with at least one
vertex, by listing S with repetitions as an s-tuple, or, if S is empty
and s ≥ 1, by a constant tuple, since every ∅-flip is also a {v}-flip. On the empty graph
there is no s-tuple for s ≥ 1, while the empty set still works. The
formulation by sets makes "s-definable implies s'-definable for s' ≥ s"
hold without exception.

# Formalization notes

An s-definable flip, `IsDefinableFlip G s H`, is defined by the second,

namespace Lax185574.DefinableFlips

open Lax185574.AtomicTypes Lax185574.Flips Lax185574.Partitions

universe u

variable {V : Type u}

/-- `G ⊕ (p̄, R)`: two distinct vertices are adjacent if and only if
their adjacency in `G` differs from membership of the pair of their
atomic types over `p̄` in the symmetric relation `R`. -/
noncomputable def flipOver (G : SimpleGraph V) {s : ℕ} (p : Fin s → V)
    (R : (Fin s → PairType) → (Fin s → PairType) → Prop) : SimpleGraph V :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun u v =>
    Xor (G.Adj u v) (R (atomicTypeOver G p u) (atomicTypeOver G p v))

/-- `H` is an `s`-definable flip of `G`: an `S`-flip of `G` for some set
`S` of at most `s` vertices. -/
def IsDefinableFlip (G : SimpleGraph V) (s : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset V, S.card ≤ s ∧ IsFlip G (atomicTypes G (S : Set V)) H

end Lax185574.DefinableFlips

concepts.title: Transitivity of definable flips
concepts.description:
Let G₁ be an s₁-definable flip of G₀ and G₂ be an s₂-definable flip of
G₁. Then G₂ is an (s₁ + s₂)-definable flip of G₀.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The three graphs share a vertex type, which may be infinite. The paper
states this as well known and refers to Lemma 2.6 in the full version
of the cited work on flipper games. With the definition of
`DefinableFlips`, the parameter set of G₂ over G₀ can be taken to be the
union of the two given parameter sets.
