namespace Lax185574.LocalToGlobal

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language
open Lax185574.FirstOrderTypes Lax185574.GaifmanGraph

universe u v z

/-- **Local-to-global types.** For a relational structure of arity at
most `α`, the type of quantifier rank `q` of a `k`-tuple is determined
by its type of quantifier rank `q'` in any induced substructure that
contains its ball of radius `7^q`. -/
axiom rankType_eq_of_rankType_induced_eq (k q α : ℕ) :
    ∃ q' : ℕ, ∀ (L : Language.{u, v}) [L.IsRelational],
      (∀ l, α < l → IsEmpty (L.Relations l)) →
      ∀ (V : Type z) [Finite V] [L.Structure V] (B B' : Set V)
        (a : Fin k → B) (b : Fin k → B'),
        ball L (7 ^ q) (Subtype.val ∘ a) ⊆ B →
        ball L (7 ^ q) (Subtype.val ∘ b) ⊆ B' →
        @rankType L B (induced B) q' k a = @rankType L B' (induced B') q' k b →
        rankType (L := L) q (Subtype.val ∘ a) = rankType (L := L) q (Subtype.val ∘ b)

end Lax185574.LocalToGlobal

concepts.title: Many atomic types force atomically matched tuples
concepts.description:
There exists a computable function Q : ℕ → ℕ such that for every ℓ ∈ ℕ
and for every bipartite graph G = (L, R, E) with |ATypes(L/R)| > Q(ℓ),
there are two tuples ā ∈ L^ℓ and b̄ ∈ R^ℓ that are atomically matched
in G.

This is Corollary 2.4 of Ding, Oporowski, Oxley and Vertigan (1996), see
also Theorem 2 of Gravier, Maffray, Renault and Trotignon (2004).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A bipartite graph (L, R, E) is given by two finite types L and R and a
relation E between them. Its graph is the simple graph on L ⊕ R whose
edges are the pairs related by E, `BipartiteGraphs.bipartiteGraph E`. The number
|ATypes(L/R)| is `AtomicTypes.atomicTypeCount` of this graph, for the
vertices of L over the vertices of R. Since L and R are disjoint, it is
the number of distinct neighborhoods of vertices of L. Computability of
Q is mathlib's `Computable`. The two sides are finite, which covers the
use in the paper inside the proof of the ball-types lemma.

namespace Lax185574.MatchedTuples

open Lax185574.AtomicMatching Lax185574.AtomicTypes Lax185574.BipartiteGraphs

universe u v

/-- **Matchings, co-matchings and half-graphs.** A computable `Q` such
that a bipartite graph whose left side realizes more than `Q(ℓ)` atomic
types over the right side contains atomically matched `ℓ`-tuples, one
from each side. -/
axiom exists_atomicallyMatched :
    ∃ Q : ℕ → ℕ, Computable Q ∧
      ∀ (ℓ : ℕ) (L : Type u) (R : Type v) [Finite L] [Finite R] (E : L → R → Prop),
        Q ℓ < atomicTypeCount (bipartiteGraph E) (Set.range Sum.inl)
            (Set.range Sum.inr) →
          ∃ (a : Fin ℓ → L) (b : Fin ℓ → R),
            AtomicallyMatched (bipartiteGraph E) (Sum.inl ∘ a) (Sum.inr ∘ b)

end Lax185574.MatchedTuples

concepts.title: Lifting type trees through a merge
concepts.description:
Fix ℓ ≤ k and q ∈ ℕ. Let G be a partial graph and ā ∈ V(G)^ℓ. Given
tree^G_{k,q}(ā) and two distinct colors P, Q, one can compute
tree^H_{k,q}(ā), where H = merge_{P,Q}(G), in time
poly_{k,q}(‖tree^G_{k,q}(ā)‖).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The merge is `Lax185574.ConstructionSequences.merge`, which recolors Q
to P. The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of
`Lax185574.Algorithms`, one for all k and q. Its input is the triple of
the type tree, P and Q. The size ‖τ‖ is the length of the encoding of
τ, and the time is `O((‖τ‖ + 1)^a)`, where the degree `a` and the
constant `c` may depend on k and q.

concepts.title: Merge sequences and their radius-r width
concepts.description:
A *merge sequence* of a graph G is a sequence (𝒫₁, R₁), …, (𝒫_m, R_m)
such that:

1. 𝒫₁ is the partition into singletons and 𝒫_m = {V(G)},
2. 𝒫₁ ≼ ⋯ ≼ 𝒫_m,
3. R₁ ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ R_m ⊆ (V(G) choose 2), and
4. for every i ∈ [m] and X, Y ∈ 𝒫_i, the set XY ∖ R_i is contained
   either in E(G) or in E(Ḡ), that is, the pair X, Y is homogeneous once
   pairs in R_i are ignored.

Here XY is the set of pairs xy with x ∈ X, y ∈ Y and x ≠ y. Condition 4
says that 𝒫_i is *homogeneous modulo R_i*. The *radius-r width* of the
merge sequence is

max_{2 ≤ i ≤ m} max_{v ∈ V(G)} |Ball^{R_i}_r(v)/𝒫_{i−1}|.

The offset in the indices of R_i and 𝒫_{i−1} is intentional.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A merge sequence is a nonempty list of pairs of a partition, as in
`Lax185574.Partitions`, and a simple graph on the vertex type, whose
edges are the pairs of R_i. So R_i ⊆ (V(G) choose 2) holds by
construction, and R_i ⊆ R_{i+1} is the subgraph order. The partition
into singletons is `⊥` and the partition with one part is `⊤`.

Homogeneity modulo R names the parts X and Y by vertices a and b with
X = 𝒫(a) and Y = 𝒫(b), as for flips in `Lax185574.Flips`. The ball
Ball^{R_i}_r(v) is the ball in the graph R_i, `GraphBalls.graphBall`.
The width is the supremum of a set of natural numbers, finite on a
finite vertex type, and the empty maximum (a sequence of length one) is
0. Algorithms exchange merge sequences as lists of pairs of a partition
and a graph, in the encodings of `Lax185574.Encodings` and

import Lax185574.Partitions
import Lax185574.GraphBalls
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Merge sequences and their radius-r width
type: definition
---
A *merge sequence* of a graph G is a sequence (𝒫₁, R₁), …, (𝒫_m, R_m)
such that:

1. 𝒫₁ is the partition into singletons and 𝒫_m = {V(G)},
2. 𝒫₁ ≼ ⋯ ≼ 𝒫_m,
3. R₁ ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ R_m ⊆ (V(G) choose 2), and
4. for every i ∈ [m] and X, Y ∈ 𝒫_i, the set XY ∖ R_i is contained
   either in E(G) or in E(Ḡ), that is, the pair X, Y is homogeneous once
   pairs in R_i are ignored.

Here XY is the set of pairs xy with x ∈ X, y ∈ Y and x ≠ y. Condition 4
says that 𝒫_i is *homogeneous modulo R_i*. The *radius-r width* of the
merge sequence is

max_{2 ≤ i ≤ m} max_{v ∈ V(G)} |Ball^{R_i}_r(v)/𝒫_{i−1}|.

The offset in the indices of R_i and 𝒫_{i−1} is intentional.

# Formalization notes

A merge sequence is a nonempty list of pairs of a partition, as in
`Lax185574.Partitions`, and a simple graph on the vertex type, whose
edges are the pairs of R_i. So R_i ⊆ (V(G) choose 2) holds by
construction, and R_i ⊆ R_{i+1} is the subgraph order. The partition
into singletons is `⊥` and the partition with one part is `⊤`.

Homogeneity modulo R names the parts X and Y by vertices a and b with
X = 𝒫(a) and Y = 𝒫(b), as for flips in `Lax185574.Flips`. The ball
Ball^{R_i}_r(v) is the ball in the graph R_i, `GraphBalls.graphBall`.
The width is the supremum of a set of natural numbers, finite on a
finite vertex type, and the empty maximum (a sequence of length one) is
0. Algorithms exchange merge sequences as lists of pairs of a partition
and a graph, in the encodings of `Lax185574.Encodings` and
`Lax185574.Partitions`.
-/

namespace Lax185574.MergeSequences

open Lax185574.Partitions Lax185574.GraphBalls

universe z

variable {V : Type z}

/-- `P` is homogeneous modulo `R`: for every pair of parts `𝒫(a)`,
`𝒫(b)`, the pairs of distinct vertices between them that are not in
`R` are all edges of `G`, or all non-edges of `G`. -/
def HomogeneousModulo (G : SimpleGraph V) (P : Setoid V) (R : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : V,
    (∀ x y : V, P x a → P y b → x ≠ y → ¬ R.Adj x y → G.Adj x y) ∨
      (∀ x y : V, P x a → P y b → x ≠ y → ¬ R.Adj x y → ¬ G.Adj x y)

/-- `ms` is a merge sequence of `G`: it starts with the partition into
singletons and ends with the partition with one part, the partitions
get coarser and the relations grow, and every partition is homogeneous
modulo its relation. -/
def IsMergeSequence (G : SimpleGraph V) (ms : List (Setoid V × SimpleGraph V)) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : ms ≠ [],
    (ms.head h).1 = ⊥ ∧ (ms.getLast h).1 = ⊤ ∧
    (∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : t + 1 < ms.length), ms[t].1 ≤ ms[t + 1].1 ∧ ms[t].2 ≤ ms[t + 1].2) ∧
    ∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : t < ms.length), HomogeneousModulo G ms[t].1 ms[t].2

/-- The radius-`r` width of the merge sequence `ms`: the largest number
of parts of `𝒫_t` that meet a ball of radius `r` in `R_{t+1}`. -/
noncomputable def mergeWidth (r : ℕ) (ms : List (Setoid V × SimpleGraph V)) : ℕ :=
  sSup {K | ∃ (t : ℕ) (ht : t + 1 < ms.length) (v : V),
    K = partCount ms[t].1 (graphBall ms[t + 1].2 r {v})}

end Lax185574.MergeSequences

concepts.title: From merge sequences to locally definable construction sequences
concepts.description:
For every n-vertex graph G and merge sequence (𝒫₁, R₁), …, (𝒫_ℓ, R_ℓ) of
G, there is a construction sequence G₁, …, G_λ of G such that the
following properties hold for all r ≥ 1. Let w_r be the radius-r width
of the merge sequence.

1. The obtained construction sequence has radius-r width at most w_r,
   and has length λ ≤ O(n w₁).
2. Suppose for every i ∈ [ℓ], the relations ≡_{𝒫_i} and R_i are
   definable in some expansion of G with 2 unary predicates, using two
   fixed first-order formulas of quantifier rank 5. Then, for every
   t ∈ [λ−1] and v ∈ V(G), the induced partial graph
   G_t[Ball^{G_{t+1}}_r(v)] is definable in some expansion of G with
   2ℓ+1 unary predicates, using formulas of quantifier rank 7 with w_r
   parameters.
3. The construction sequence can be computed in time O(ℓ n²), given an
   n-vertex graph G and merge sequence of length ℓ.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The construction sequence is produced by a function `script` of the
graph and the merge sequence, as a script of
`Lax185574.ConstructionSequences`, and the algorithm `A` computes this
function, in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`. The algorithm, the
constant `c` of the time bound O((ℓ+1) · (n+1)²) and the constant `K` of
the length bound come first, so both constants are absolute. The input
is the pair (G, merge sequence). A graph has the vertices `Fin n`, and
the notions of merge sequences and construction sequences are applied
to its `SimpleGraph`.

A merge sequence is one in the sense of `Lax185574.MergeSequences`, so
𝒫₁ is the partition into singletons and 𝒫_ℓ = {V(G)} by its definition.

The width of item 1 is the radius-r width of
`Lax185574.ConstructionWidth`, which counts parts. The length bound
O(n w₁) is spelled out as K · (n+1) · (w₁+1). The radius-r width of the
merge sequence is `MergeSequences.mergeWidth`. The definability
hypothesis of item 2 is `BetterMergeSequences.StagesDefinable` for some
two formulas of quantifier rank at most 5, and the conclusion is
`LocalDefinability.IsRadiusDefinable` with 2ℓ+1 predicates, w_r
parameters and rank 7.

**Deviation from the paper.** Both bounds use max(1, w_r) instead of
w_r. On a graph with one vertex the merge sequence of length 1 has width
0, the maximum over an empty range, while every construction sequence
has width 1. For n ≥ 2 the two agree, since every merge sequence has
length at least 2 and width at least 1.

Every number in the encoding of the script is at most the length of the
encoding plus n (`Script.HasSmallNumbers`). The paper does not say
this. An algorithm can ensure it by giving the vertices of the initial
partial graph the colors 0, …, n − 1. The bound lets the output be
passed on as in `Lax185574.DefinableSequences`.

namespace Lax185574.MergeToConstruction

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Lax710763.Transductions
open Lax185574.Graphs Lax185574.Algorithms
open Lax185574.Partitions Lax185574.MergeSequences Lax185574.BetterMergeSequences
open Lax185574.ConstructionSequences Lax185574.ConstructionWidth

/-- **Merge sequences to construction sequences.** One algorithm
converts a merge sequence of length `ℓ` of a graph into a construction
sequence of the same graph, given by its script, in time
`O((ℓ+1) · (n+1)²)`. For every `r ≥ 1`, the construction sequence has
radius-`r` width at most `max 1 w_r`, where `w_r` is the radius-`r`
width of the merge sequence, and length at most `K · (n+1) · (w₁+1)`. If
two formulas of quantifier rank at most `5` define the stages, it is
radius-`r` definable with `2ℓ+1` predicates, `max 1 w_r` parameters and
rank `7`. -/
axiom exists_constructionSequence_of_mergeSequence :
    ∃ (A : Algorithm) (c K : ℕ) (script : (G : Graph) →
        List (Setoid (Fin G.n) × SimpleGraph (Fin G.n)) → Script G.n),
      ∀ (G : Graph) (ms : List (Setoid (Fin G.n) × SimpleGraph (Fin G.n))),
        IsMergeSequence G.toSimpleGraph ms →
          let σ := script G ms
          IsConstructionSequence G.toSimpleGraph σ.run ∧ σ.HasSmallNumbers ∧
          σ.run.length ≤ K * (G.n + 1) * (mergeWidth 1 ms + 1) ∧
          (∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r →
            constructionWidth r σ.run ≤ max 1 (mergeWidth r ms) ∧
            ((∃ φeq φR : (withColors Language.graph 2).Formula (Fin 2),
                quantifierRank φeq ≤ 5 ∧ quantifierRank φR ≤ 5 ∧
                  StagesDefinable G.toSimpleGraph ms φeq φR) →
              IsRadiusDefinable G.toSimpleGraph σ.run r (2 * ms.length + 1)
                (max 1 (mergeWidth r ms)) 7)) ∧
          A.Computes c (G, ms) σ ((ms.length + 1) * (G.n + 1) ^ 2)

end Lax185574.MergeToConstruction

concepts.title: First-order model checking on monadically dependent graph classes
concepts.description:
There is an algorithm which solves the model checking problem for
first-order logic on graphs, that is, it decides whether a given graph
*G* satisfies a given first-order sentence φ, with the following
guarantee. For every monadically dependent graph class 𝒞 and every real
ε > 0, the algorithm runs in time O_{𝒞,φ,ε}(n^(3+ε)) on the n-vertex
graphs G ∈ 𝒞.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`, a
word RAM program together with the exponent of the word length it needs.
It comes first, before the class, the sentence and ε, and it knows none
of them. Only the constant `c` of the O-notation depends on them.

`A.Decides c (G, φ) (G ⊨ φ) T` is a statement about the encoding of the
pair `(G, φ)` of `Lax185574.Encodings`, which is the encoding of the
graph followed by the encoding of the sentence. At every word length
that is admissible for `c`, every halting run of `A` on this input
writes `1` if `G ⊨ φ` and `0` otherwise, and `A` halts within
`c · T + c` steps once this number fits into a word. Here
`T = n^(3+ε)` is the real power. The additive `c` is part of the
O-notation, and it covers small graphs, such as the graph without
vertices, where `T` vanishes. An n-vertex graph with m edges is encoded
by a word of length n + 4m + 1 ≤ 2n² + 1, so reading the input fits into
the time bound.

Every graph lies in a monadically dependent class, for instance the
class consisting of it alone. So the algorithm decides every instance
correctly at every word length that is admissible for some such class.
The time bound is claimed for members of a monadically dependent class
only.

Monadic dependence is the transduction-based definition of
`Lax185574.MonadicDependence`: the class does not transduce the class of
all graphs. It agrees with the archive's definition
`Lax710763.MonadicDependence` and with the definition of the paper, see
`Lax185574.MonadicDependence`.

concepts.title: Monadically dependent graph classes
concepts.description:
A graph class C *transduces the class of all graphs* if there are a
number k and a first-order formula ψ(x₀, x₁) with k colors such that
every graph H can be found inside a k-colored graph from C, with ψ
defining the edges of H. That is, there are a graph G ∈ C, a coloring of
G with k colors, and an injective map f from the vertices of H to the
vertices of G such that for all distinct vertices u and v of H

  u and v are adjacent in H ⟺ ψ(f(u), f(v)) holds in the colored G.

The class C is *monadically dependent* if it does not transduce the
class of all graphs.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
This is the transduction-based definition of monadic dependence. A
general transduction also has a domain formula, which selects the
vertices of the output graph. It is not needed here, because the vertex
set of H is the image of f, and the class of all graphs is closed under
induced subgraphs. A transduction with domain formula δ(x) and edge
formula ψ that produces every graph gives an f as above (map H to the
vertices of its copy that δ selects). Conversely, f gives the
transduction whose domain formula is a fresh color marking the image of
f and whose edge formula is ψ(x₀, x₁) ∧ x₀ ≠ x₁. The conjunct x₀ ≠ x₁ is
needed because the condition above constrains ψ on distinct vertices
only, while the edge formula of a transduction defines the adjacency on
all pairs of selected vertices, and a vertex is not adjacent to itself.

The definition of the paper is of this form. It starts from a formula
φ(x, y), takes the graph with the edges uv such that φ(u, v) or φ(v, u)
holds, and asks for every finite graph as an induced subgraph. Such a φ
gives ψ = φ(x₀, x₁) ∨ φ(x₁, x₀) here. Conversely, a ψ as above serves as
φ, since on the image of f it holds of u and v in both orders or in
neither. So the two definitions agree.

Monadic dependence is often defined by forbidding the independence
property for formulas on the colorings of the graphs in C. By a theorem
of Baldwin and Shelah the two definitions agree.

/-- The class `C` transduces the class of all graphs: some formula
`ψ(x₀, x₁)` with `k` colors defines every graph `H` on the image of an
injective map `f` into some `k`-colored graph `G ∈ C`. -/
def TransducesAllGraphs (C : GraphClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (ψ : Formula (Fin k) 2),
    ∀ H : Graph, ∃ G ∈ C, ∃ (col : Fin k → Set (Fin G.n)) (f : Fin H.n ↪ Fin G.n),
      ∀ u v : Fin H.n, u ≠ v → (H.Adj u v ↔ ψ.Holds G col ![f u, f v])

/-- A graph class is monadically dependent if it does not transduce the
class of all graphs. -/
def MonadicallyDependent (C : GraphClass) : Prop :=
  ¬ TransducesAllGraphs C

end Lax185574.MonadicDependence

concepts.title: Polynomial neighborhood complexity from bounded VC-dimension
concepts.description:
If G has VC-dimension d then

π_G(k) ≤ (k + 1)^d  for all k ∈ ℕ.

This follows from the Sauer–Shelah lemma.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The hypothesis is VC-dimension at most d, which is equivalent: a graph
of VC-dimension d' ≤ d satisfies the bound for d', hence for d. The
graph may be infinite. Its VC-dimension is then an extended natural
number, and the hypothesis excludes the value ⊤.

concepts.title: Pairs at distance at most 5 in both polarities
concepts.description:
Let G be a graph and 𝒫 a partition of V = V(G). Define
R = R(G, 𝒫) ⊆ (V choose 2) so that for all parts X, Y ∈ 𝒫 (possibly
X = Y) and pairs uv with u ∈ X, v ∈ Y and u ≠ v, we have uv ∈ R if and
only if

dist^{G[X,Y]}(u, v) ≤ 5  and  dist^{Ḡ[X,Y]}(u, v) ≤ 5.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The relation is a simple graph on V. For a pair uv the parts are
X = 𝒫(u) and Y = 𝒫(v), and the distances are those from the left copy of
u to the right copy of v in the graphs `pairGraph G X Y` and
`coPairGraph G X Y` of `Lax185574.BipartiteGraphs`, measured by walks.
When X = Y the vertices u and v lie in opposite copies of X, as in the
paper. `SimpleGraph.fromRel` removes the pairs with u = v and
symmetrizes. The condition is already symmetric in u and v, since
exchanging the two copies of V maps G[X, Y] to G[Y, X].

namespace Lax185574.PairRelation

open Lax185574.BipartiteGraphs Lax185574.Partitions Lax185574.GaifmanGraph

universe z

variable {V : Type z}

/-- The relation `R(G, 𝒫)`: distinct `u` and `v` are related if they
are within distance `5` both in `G[𝒫(u), 𝒫(v)]` and in
`Ḡ[𝒫(u), 𝒫(v)]`. -/
def pairRelation (G : SimpleGraph V) (P : Setoid V) : SimpleGraph V :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun u v =>
    WithinDist (pairGraph G (part P u) (part P v)) 5 (.inl u) (.inr v) ∧
      WithinDist (coPairGraph G (part P u) (part P v)) 5 (.inl u) (.inr v)

end Lax185574.PairRelation

concepts.title: Balls of the pair relation lie in flip-metric balls
concepts.description:
Fix a graph G and a partition 𝒫 of V(G), and let R ≔ R(G, 𝒫). For every
radius r ∈ ℕ and vertex v ∈ V(G),

Ball^R_r(v) ⊆ Ball^𝒫_{5r}(v).

sections.title: Formalization notes

Ball^R_r(v) is the ball in the graph R, `GraphBalls.graphBall`, around
the single vertex v. Ball^𝒫_{5r}(v) is the ball of the 𝒫-flip metric,
`Flips.flipBall`.

concepts.title: The pair relation of atomic types is definable
concepts.description:
Suppose G is a graph and 𝒫 is the partition of V(G) into atomic types
over some set S ⊆ V(G). Then the relation R ≔ R(G, 𝒫) is definable in G
expanded with one unary predicate marking S, using a fixed first-order
formula φ_R(x, y) of quantifier rank at most 5.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
"Fixed" means that one formula serves all graphs and all sets S, so the
formula is chosen first. It is a formula of graphs with one color, in
the language of `Lax185574.Colorings`, with the two free variables x
and y of `Fin 2`. The expansion interprets the color by S. The graph may
be infinite.

/-- **Definability of the pair relation.** One formula of quantifier

      ∀ {V : Type z} (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Set V) (x : Fin 2 → V),
        @Formula.Realize _ V (expansion G fun _ => S) _ φ x ↔

concepts.title: The pair relation grows under coarsening
concepts.description:
Fix a graph G and partitions 𝒫 and 𝒫′ of V(G) such that 𝒫 refines 𝒫′.
Then R(G, 𝒫) ⊆ R(G, 𝒫′).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The relation R(G, 𝒫) is `PairRelation.pairRelation`, a simple graph,
and inclusion is the subgraph order. On two copies of V(G), the graph
G[X, Y] is a subgraph of G[X′, Y′] whenever X ⊆ X′ and Y ⊆ Y′, also
when X ≠ Y and X′ = Y′, and likewise for Ḡ[X, Y]. The proof in the
paper says more, that G[X, Y] is an induced subgraph of G[X′, Y′].
Distances only need the subgraph relation.

concepts.title: Partial graphs
concepts.description:
A *partial graph* H consists of a finite vertex set V = V(H), two
disjoint sets E(H), N(H) ⊆ (V choose 2) of *edges* and *non-edges*, and
a partition of V whose parts are treated as colors. The pairs in
R(H) = E(H) ∪ N(H) are *resolved*, and all other pairs are
*unresolved*. H is viewed as a logical structure with binary relations E
and N and a unary predicate for every color. Distances dist^H and balls
Ball^H_r(v) are measured in the Gaifman graph (V, R(H)), the graph of
resolved pairs.

For the model-checking algorithm, the parts are given names, to track
them over time. Fix a countably infinite set of unary symbols, called
*colors*. A partial graph G is regarded as a relational structure with
the two symmetric binary relations E and N and a unary relation Y for
every color Y. The vertices of color Y form its *color class* Y^G, and
the nonempty color classes are the *parts* of G. The size of the
representation of G is given by |G| = |V(G)| and
‖G‖ = |V(G)| + |R(G)|.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The paper introduces partial graphs in the technical overview and
extends the notion in the preliminaries of the model-checking part. Both
passages describe the same objects. All metric notions count resolved
pairs, edges and non-edges alike.

Colors are natural numbers. Edges and non-edges are simple graphs on the
vertex type, so they are symmetric and irreflexive by construction, and
a resolved pair is an edge of their supremum. The language of partial
graphs has the two binary symbols and one unary symbol per natural
number. Its Gaifman graph is exactly the graph of resolved pairs. That
graph is what `ball` uses, so `ball` agrees with
`Lax185574.GaifmanGraph.ball` on the structure of a partial graph.

The induced partial graph G[X], defined in the paper together with
`Lax185574.ConstructionWidth`, is the induced substructure of
`Lax185574.GaifmanGraph`, applied to the structure of G. Statements
about G[X] do not use this substructure. They are stated through the
partial graph G and the set X, see `Lax185574.LocalDefinability`, and
need no separate definition.

For a partial graph on `Fin n`, |G| is `n`. The size ‖G‖ =
|V(G)| + |R(G)|, used in running-time bounds, is `PartialGraph.size`.

The distance matrix D_G of a partial graph, with entries
D_G(u, v) = dist^G(u, v) ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}, is `Lax185574.DistanceMatrix`. It is
∞ for vertices in different components of the graph of resolved pairs.
The algorithms of the model-checking procedure receive it as an
additional input, and maintain it along the construction sequence.

namespace Lax185574.PartialGraphs

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language
open Lax185574.GaifmanGraph

universe z

/-- A partial graph on the vertex type `V`: disjoint edges and
non-edges, and one color per vertex. -/
structure PartialGraph (V : Type z) where
  /-- The edges `E(G)`. -/
  edge : SimpleGraph V
  /-- The non-edges `N(G)`. -/
  nonEdge : SimpleGraph V
  /-- No pair is both an edge and a non-edge. -/
  disjoint : Disjoint edge nonEdge
  /-- The color of each vertex. -/
  color : V → ℕ

variable {V : Type z}

namespace PartialGraph

/-- The resolved pairs `R(G) = E(G) ∪ N(G)`, the Gaifman graph of the
partial graph. -/
def resolved (G : PartialGraph V) : SimpleGraph V := G.edge ⊔ G.nonEdge

/-- `Ball^G_r(v)`: the vertices within distance `r` of `v` along
resolved pairs. -/
def ball (G : PartialGraph V) (r : ℕ) (v : V) : Set V :=
  {u | WithinDist G.resolved r v u}

/-- The color class `Y^G`. -/
def colorClass (G : PartialGraph V) (Y : ℕ) : Set V := {v | G.color v = Y}

/-- The size `‖G‖ = |V(G)| + |R(G)|` of a partial graph on `Fin n`. -/
noncomputable def size {n : ℕ} (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  n + Set.ncard G.resolved.edgeSet

end PartialGraph

/-- The relation symbols of partial graphs: edges, non-edges and one
unary symbol per color. -/
inductive Rel : ℕ → Type
  | edge : Rel 2
  | nonEdge : Rel 2
  | color (Y : ℕ) : Rel 1

/-- The language of partial graphs. -/
def language : Language :=
  ⟨fun _ => Empty, Rel⟩
  deriving Language.IsRelational

/-- A partial graph as a relational structure. -/
@[implicit_reducible]
def PartialGraph.structure (G : PartialGraph V) : language.Structure V where
  funMap f := isEmptyElim f
  RelMap
    | .edge => fun x => G.edge.Adj (x 0) (x 1)
    | .nonEdge => fun x => G.nonEdge.Adj (x 0) (x 1)
    | .color Y => fun x => G.color (x 0) = Y

open Lax185574.Encoding in
/-- A partial graph on `Fin n` is encoded by the family of its colors,
then its edges and then its non-edges, each graph as in
`Lax185574.Encodings`. So the encoding is `n` and the `n` colors, then
`n` and for every vertex in order the set of its neighbors along edges,
then `n` and for every vertex the set of its neighbors along non-edges.
It is determined by the partial graph and has length O(‖G‖). Running
times are stated in terms of ‖G‖, which is only meaningful for an
encoding without padding. The edges and non-edges are relations, so the
encoding is not derived. -/
noncomputable instance {n : ℕ} : Encode (PartialGraph (Fin n)) where
  encode G := encode (G.color, G.edge, G.nonEdge)

end Lax185574.PartialGraphs

concepts.title: Converting the flip metric of a partition into a single flip
concepts.description:
Let G be a graph and let 𝒫 be a partition of V(G). There is a refinement
𝒬 of 𝒫 with |𝒬| ≤ |𝒫| · 2^|𝒫| and a 𝒬-flip H of G such that, for every
v ∈ V(G) and r ∈ ℕ,

Ball^H_r(v) ⊆ Ball^𝒫_{6r}(v).

This is Lemma 8 of the cited work on separability properties of
monadically dependent graph classes.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The graph is finite, so the numbers of parts are natural numbers, the
cardinalities of the quotients. The refinement 𝒬 and the flip H are
chosen once, before the vertex v and the radius r. The ball Ball^H_r(v)
is `GraphBalls.graphBall H r {v}`, and Ball^𝒫_{6r}(v) is the flip-metric
ball `Flips.flipBall`.

/-!
---
title: Converting the flip metric of a partition into a single flip
type: lemma
---
Let G be a graph and let 𝒫 be a partition of V(G). There is a refinement
𝒬 of 𝒫 with |𝒬| ≤ |𝒫| · 2^|𝒫| and a 𝒬-flip H of G such that, for every
v ∈ V(G) and r ∈ ℕ,

Ball^H_r(v) ⊆ Ball^𝒫_{6r}(v).

This is Lemma 8 of the cited work on separability properties of
monadically dependent graph classes.

# Formalization notes

The graph is finite, so the numbers of parts are natural numbers, the
cardinalities of the quotients. The refinement 𝒬 and the flip H are
chosen once, before the vertex v and the radius r. The ball Ball^H_r(v)
is `GraphBalls.graphBall H r {v}`, and Ball^𝒫_{6r}(v) is the flip-metric
ball `Flips.flipBall`.
-/

namespace Lax185574.PartitionMetricConversion

open Lax185574.Flips Lax185574.GraphBalls

universe u

/-- **Partition-metric conversion.** A refinement `𝒬` of `𝒫` with at
most `|𝒫| · 2^|𝒫|` parts carries a single flip whose radius-`r` balls lie
in the radius-`6r` balls of the flip metric of `𝒫`. -/
axiom exists_refinement_flip {V : Type u} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (P : Setoid V) :
    ∃ Q : Setoid V, Q ≤ P ∧
      Nat.card (Quotient Q) ≤ Nat.card (Quotient P) * 2 ^ Nat.card (Quotient P) ∧
      ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, IsFlip G Q H ∧
        ∀ (v : V) (r : ℕ), graphBall H r {v} ⊆ flipBall G P (6 * r) v

end Lax185574.PartitionMetricConversion

exists_refinement_flip : ∀ {V : Type u} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (P : Setoid V),
  Exists fun Q =>
    And (Setoid.instLE_mathlib.le Q P)
      (And
        (instLENat.le (Nat.card (Quotient Q))
          (instHMul.hMul (Nat.card (Quotient P)) (instHPow.hPow 2 (Nat.card (Quotient P)))))
        (Exists fun H =>
          And (Lax185574.Flips.IsFlip G Q H)
            (∀ (v : V) (r : Nat),
              Set.instLE.le (Lax185574.GraphBalls.graphBall H r (Set.instSingletonSet.singleton v))
                (Lax185574.Flips.flipBall G P (instHMul.hMul 6 r) v))))
statements.doc:
**Partition-metric conversion.** A refinement `𝒬` of `𝒫` with at
most `|𝒫| · 2^|𝒫|` parts carries a single flip whose radius-`r` balls lie
in the radius-`6r` balls of the flip metric of `𝒫`.

concepts.title: Partitions, transversals and the partition into atomic types
concepts.description:
For two partitions 𝒫, 𝒬 of the same set, 𝒫 ≼ 𝒬 says that 𝒫 refines 𝒬,
that is, each part of 𝒫 is contained in some part of 𝒬. For a partition
𝒫 of V and X ⊆ V, X/𝒫 is the set of parts of 𝒫 that meet X. The part of
𝒫 containing an element v is 𝒫(v). Further, ≡_𝒫 is the equivalence
relation on V whose classes are the parts of 𝒫. A *transversal* of 𝒫 is
a set that contains exactly one vertex of every part.

For a graph G and S ⊆ V(G), two vertices u, v have the same atomic type
over S if and only if either u = v, or u, v ∉ S and N(u) ∩ S = N(v) ∩ S.
The *partition into atomic types* 𝒫_S partitions S into singletons and
the vertices of V(G) ∖ S according to their neighborhoods in S.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A partition of V is an equivalence relation on V, a `Setoid V`. Its
parts are the equivalence classes, so ≡_𝒫 is the relation itself and
𝒫 ≼ 𝒬 is the order `P ≤ Q` of setoids. The partition into singletons is
`⊥`, and the partition with one part is `⊤`. The number |X/𝒫| is the
number of classes of elements of X, `partCount`. It is the exact count
on a finite vertex type, which is the case in every statement that uses
it.

The partition into atomic types is the kernel of the map
v ↦ (S ∩ {v}, S ∩ N(v)). Two vertices have the same image exactly when
they are equal, or both lie outside S and have the same neighborhood in
S. So this is the partition of the paper. It is also the partition
into types of quantifier rank 0 over S in the sense of
`Lax185574.FirstOrderTypes`, which the paper mentions as the definition.

Algorithms exchange partitions of `Fin n` as the finite set of their
parts, each part a finite set of vertices, in the encodings of
`Lax185574.Encodings`. This is the instance below.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax185574.Encodings
import Mathlib.Data.Setoid.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic

/-!
---
title: Partitions, transversals and the partition into atomic types
type: definition
---
For two partitions 𝒫, 𝒬 of the same set, 𝒫 ≼ 𝒬 says that 𝒫 refines 𝒬,
that is, each part of 𝒫 is contained in some part of 𝒬. For a partition
𝒫 of V and X ⊆ V, X/𝒫 is the set of parts of 𝒫 that meet X. The part of
𝒫 containing an element v is 𝒫(v). Further, ≡_𝒫 is the equivalence
relation on V whose classes are the parts of 𝒫. A *transversal* of 𝒫 is
a set that contains exactly one vertex of every part.

For a graph G and S ⊆ V(G), two vertices u, v have the same atomic type
over S if and only if either u = v, or u, v ∉ S and N(u) ∩ S = N(v) ∩ S.
The *partition into atomic types* 𝒫_S partitions S into singletons and
the vertices of V(G) ∖ S according to their neighborhoods in S.

# Formalization notes

A partition of V is an equivalence relation on V, a `Setoid V`. Its
parts are the equivalence classes, so ≡_𝒫 is the relation itself and
𝒫 ≼ 𝒬 is the order `P ≤ Q` of setoids. The partition into singletons is
`⊥`, and the partition with one part is `⊤`. The number |X/𝒫| is the
number of classes of elements of X, `partCount`. It is the exact count
on a finite vertex type, which is the case in every statement that uses
it.

The partition into atomic types is the kernel of the map
v ↦ (S ∩ {v}, S ∩ N(v)). Two vertices have the same image exactly when
they are equal, or both lie outside S and have the same neighborhood in
S. So this is the partition of the paper. It is also the partition
into types of quantifier rank 0 over S in the sense of
`Lax185574.FirstOrderTypes`, which the paper mentions as the definition.

Algorithms exchange partitions of `Fin n` as the finite set of their
parts, each part a finite set of vertices, in the encodings of
`Lax185574.Encodings`. This is the instance below.
-/

namespace Lax185574.Partitions

open Lax185574.Encoding

universe z

variable {V : Type z}

/-- `|X/𝒫|`: the number of parts of `P` that meet `X`. -/
noncomputable def partCount (P : Setoid V) (X : Set V) : ℕ :=
  (Quotient.mk P '' X).ncard

/-- The part `𝒫(v)` of `P` that contains `v`. -/
def part (P : Setoid V) (v : V) : Set V := {u | P u v}

/-- `T` is a transversal of `P`: every part of `P` contains exactly one
vertex of `T`. -/
def IsTransversal (P : Setoid V) (T : Set V) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : V, ∃! t : V, t ∈ T ∧ P t v

/-- The partition `𝒫_S` into atomic types over `S`: vertices of `S` are
singletons, and vertices outside `S` are grouped by their neighborhood
in `S`. -/
def atomicTypes (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Set V) : Setoid V :=
  Setoid.ker fun v => (S ∩ {v}, S ∩ G.neighborSet v)

/-- The parts of a partition of `Fin n`, as a finite set of finite
sets. -/
noncomputable def parts {n : ℕ} (P : Setoid (Fin n)) : Finset (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  open Classical in Finset.univ.image fun v => Finset.univ.filter fun u => P u v

/-- A partition of `Fin n` is encoded by the finite set of its parts.
A setoid is a relation, so the encoding is not derived. -/
noncomputable instance {n : ℕ} : Encode (Setoid (Fin n)) where
  encode P := encode (parts P)

end Lax185574.Partitions

concepts.title: φ-patterns
concepts.description:
For a first-order formula φ(x̄, z), a *φ-pattern* is a (φ, ψ)-pattern
with ψ(y, z) = E(y, z) or ψ(y, z) = ¬E(y, z). These are called a
*(φ, E)-pattern* and a *(φ, ¬E)-pattern*, respectively. Such a pattern
consists of tuples ā₁, …, ā_s ∈ V(G)^{|x̄|}, vertices b₁, …, b_t ∈ V(G)
and (c_{i,j} : i ∈ [s], j ∈ [t]). The tuple b̄ = (b₁, …, b_t) is the
*base* of the pattern.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The formula E(y, z) is the adjacency atom with y the single variable of
the left summand and z the variable of the right summand, as in
`PhiPsiPatterns`. A φ-pattern is a pattern for this formula or for its
negation. The base vertex bⱼ is the single entry of the tuple b̄ⱼ of
length one.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax185574.PhiPsiPatterns

/-!
---
title: φ-patterns
type: definition
---
For a first-order formula φ(x̄, z), a *φ-pattern* is a (φ, ψ)-pattern
with ψ(y, z) = E(y, z) or ψ(y, z) = ¬E(y, z). These are called a
*(φ, E)-pattern* and a *(φ, ¬E)-pattern*, respectively. Such a pattern
consists of tuples ā₁, …, ā_s ∈ V(G)^{|x̄|}, vertices b₁, …, b_t ∈ V(G)
and (c_{i,j} : i ∈ [s], j ∈ [t]). The tuple b̄ = (b₁, …, b_t) is the
*base* of the pattern.

# Formalization notes

The formula E(y, z) is the adjacency atom with y the single variable of
the left summand and z the variable of the right summand, as in
`PhiPsiPatterns`. A φ-pattern is a pattern for this formula or for its
negation. The base vertex bⱼ is the single entry of the tuple b̄ⱼ of
length one.
-/

namespace Lax185574.PhiPatterns

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language
open Lax185574.PhiPsiPatterns

universe u

variable {V : Type u}

/-- The formula `E(y, z)`. -/
def edgeFormula : Language.graph.Formula (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 1) :=
  Relations.formula₂ Language.adj (Term.var (Sum.inl 0)) (Term.var (Sum.inr 0))

/-- `G` contains a `φ`-pattern of order `s × t`: a `(φ, E)`-pattern or a
`(φ, ¬E)`-pattern. -/
def HasPhiPattern (G : SimpleGraph V) {p : ℕ}
    (φ : Language.graph.Formula (Fin p ⊕ Fin 1)) (s t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  HasPattern G φ edgeFormula s t ∨ HasPattern G φ edgeFormula.not s t

end Lax185574.PhiPatterns

concepts.title: (φ, ψ)-patterns
concepts.description:
Fix first-order formulas φ(x̄, z) and ψ(ȳ, z). A *(φ, ψ)-pattern* of
order s × t in a graph G consists of tuples ā₁, …, ā_s ∈ V(G)^{|x̄|},
b̄₁, …, b̄_t ∈ V(G)^{|ȳ|}, and vertices (c_{i,j} : i ∈ [s], j ∈ [t])
such that the following holds for all i, i' ∈ [s] and j, j' ∈ [t]:

1. G ⊨ φ(āᵢ, c_{i,j}), and G ⊭ φ(ā_{i'}, c_{i,j}) if i' > i,
2. G ⊨ ψ(b̄ⱼ, c_{i,j}), and G ⊭ ψ(b̄_{j'}, c_{i,j}) if j' > j.

The set { c_{i,j} : i ∈ [s], j ∈ [t] } is the set of *grid-points* of
the pattern, and s is its *height*.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Formulas are mathlib's first-order formulas in the language of graphs,
evaluated in the structure of the graph G. A formula φ(x̄, z) has the
free variables `Fin p ⊕ Fin 1`: the left summand is the tuple x̄ of
length p, and the right summand is the single variable z. This is the
convention of `IndependenceProperty` for formulas φ(x̄, ȳ). Rows and
columns are indexed by `Fin s` and `Fin t` with their usual order. The
grid-points and the tuples need not be distinct.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Graph
import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Semantics

/-!
---
title: (φ, ψ)-patterns
type: definition
---
Fix first-order formulas φ(x̄, z) and ψ(ȳ, z). A *(φ, ψ)-pattern* of
order s × t in a graph G consists of tuples ā₁, …, ā_s ∈ V(G)^{|x̄|},
b̄₁, …, b̄_t ∈ V(G)^{|ȳ|}, and vertices (c_{i,j} : i ∈ [s], j ∈ [t])
such that the following holds for all i, i' ∈ [s] and j, j' ∈ [t]:

1. G ⊨ φ(āᵢ, c_{i,j}), and G ⊭ φ(ā_{i'}, c_{i,j}) if i' > i,
2. G ⊨ ψ(b̄ⱼ, c_{i,j}), and G ⊭ ψ(b̄_{j'}, c_{i,j}) if j' > j.

The set { c_{i,j} : i ∈ [s], j ∈ [t] } is the set of *grid-points* of
the pattern, and s is its *height*.

# Formalization notes

Formulas are mathlib's first-order formulas in the language of graphs,
evaluated in the structure of the graph G. A formula φ(x̄, z) has the
free variables `Fin p ⊕ Fin 1`: the left summand is the tuple x̄ of
length p, and the right summand is the single variable z. This is the
convention of `IndependenceProperty` for formulas φ(x̄, ȳ). Rows and
columns are indexed by `Fin s` and `Fin t` with their usual order. The
grid-points and the tuples need not be distinct.
-/

namespace Lax185574.PhiPsiPatterns

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u

variable {V : Type u}

/-- `G ⊨ φ(ā, c)` for a formula `φ(x̄, z)` of the language of graphs. -/
def Holds (G : SimpleGraph V) {p : ℕ}
    (φ : Language.graph.Formula (Fin p ⊕ Fin 1)) (a : Fin p → V) (c : V) :
    Prop :=
  @Formula.Realize Language.graph V G.structure _ φ (Sum.elim a ![c])

/-- The tuples `a i`, `b j` and the vertices `c i j` form a
`(φ, ψ)`-pattern of order `s × t` in `G`. -/
def IsPattern (G : SimpleGraph V) {p p' : ℕ}
    (φ : Language.graph.Formula (Fin p ⊕ Fin 1))
    (ψ : Language.graph.Formula (Fin p' ⊕ Fin 1)) {s t : ℕ}
    (a : Fin s → Fin p → V) (b : Fin t → Fin p' → V) (c : Fin s → Fin t → V) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ i j,
    (Holds G φ (a i) (c i j) ∧ ∀ i', i < i' → ¬ Holds G φ (a i') (c i j)) ∧
    (Holds G ψ (b j) (c i j) ∧ ∀ j', j < j' → ¬ Holds G ψ (b j') (c i j))

/-- `G` contains a `(φ, ψ)`-pattern of order `s × t`. -/
def HasPattern (G : SimpleGraph V) {p p' : ℕ}
    (φ : Language.graph.Formula (Fin p ⊕ Fin 1))
    (ψ : Language.graph.Formula (Fin p' ⊕ Fin 1)) (s t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a : Fin s → Fin p → V) (b : Fin t → Fin p' → V) (c : Fin s → Fin t → V),
    IsPattern G φ ψ a b c

end Lax185574.PhiPsiPatterns

concepts.title: Rank shift of type trees
concepts.description:
There is a polynomial-time algorithm which maps tree_{k,q}(ā) to
tree_{k+1,q−1}(ā) for all k ∈ ℕ, q ≥ 1, partial graphs G and nonempty
ā ∈ V(G)^{≤k}.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`,
one for all k and q. Polynomial time means time `O((N + 1)^a)` on an
input of length `N`, where the degree `a` and the constant `c` may
depend on k and q. The paper says polynomial time, with no subscript,
so this is weaker than a degree independent of k and q. It suffices,
since k and q are fixed in every use. q ≥ 1 is written as q + 1.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax185574.TypeTrees
import Lax185574.Algorithms

/-!
---
title: Rank shift of type trees
type: lemma
---
There is a polynomial-time algorithm which maps tree_{k,q}(ā) to
tree_{k+1,q−1}(ā) for all k ∈ ℕ, q ≥ 1, partial graphs G and nonempty
ā ∈ V(G)^{≤k}.

# Formalization notes

The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`,
one for all k and q. Polynomial time means time `O((N + 1)^a)` on an
input of length `N`, where the degree `a` and the constant `c` may
depend on k and q. The paper says polynomial time, with no subscript,
so this is weaker than a degree independent of k and q. It suffices,
since k and q are fixed in every use. q ≥ 1 is written as q + 1.
-/

namespace Lax185574.RankShift

open Lax185574.Encoding Lax185574.Algorithms
open Lax185574.PartialGraphs Lax185574.TypeTrees

/-- **Rank shift.** One algorithm computes `tree_{k+1,q}(u)` from
`tree_{k,q+1}(u)` in polynomial time. -/
axiom exists_program_shift :
    ∃ A : Algorithm, ∀ k q : ℕ, ∃ c a : ℕ,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (ℓ : ℕ) (u : Fin ℓ → Fin n), 1 ≤ ℓ → ℓ ≤ k →
        A.Computes c (tree G k (q + 1) u) (tree G (k + 1) q u)
          (((encode (tree G k (q + 1) u)).length + 1) ^ a)

end Lax185574.RankShift

statements.signature:
exists_program_shift : Exists fun A =>
  ∀ (k q : Nat),
    Exists fun c =>
      Exists fun a =>
        ∀ (n : Nat) (G : Lax185574.PartialGraphs.PartialGraph (Fin n)) (ℓ : Nat) (u : Fin ℓ → Fin n),
          instLENat.le 1 ℓ →
            instLENat.le ℓ k →
              A.Computes c (Lax185574.TypeTrees.tree G k (instHAdd.hAdd q 1) u)
                (Lax185574.TypeTrees.tree G (instHAdd.hAdd k 1) q u)
                (instHPow.hPow
                  (instHAdd.hAdd
                    (Lax185574.TypeTrees.instEncodeTypeTree.encode
                          (Lax185574.TypeTrees.tree G k (instHAdd.hAdd q 1) u)).length.cast
                    1)
                  a)

concepts.title: Lifting type trees through a resolve
concepts.description:
Let k ≥ 1 and q ∈ ℕ. Given a partial graph G, its distance matrix D_G,
colors P, Q, a sign ±, and (tree^G_{k,q}(a) : a ∈ V(G)), one can compute
H = resolve^±_{P,Q}(G), its distance matrix D_H, and
(tree^H_{k,q}(a) : a ∈ V(G)) in time

  |G|² · poly_{k,q}(M + T),

where

  M = max_{a ∈ V(G)} ‖tree^G_{k,q}(a)‖,
  T = max_{a ∈ V(G)} |{tree^G_{k+i,q−i}(v̄) | 0 ≤ i ≤ q, ℓ ∈ [k+i],
                       v̄ ∈ (Ball^H_{ρ⁺(k,q)}(a))^ℓ}|.

Each output tree has size poly_{k,q}(T).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`,
one for all k and q. Its input is the tuple of G, its distance matrix,
P, Q, the sign and the family of type trees, with the encodings of
`Lax185574.Encodings`. The sign is a Boolean, `true` for + and `false`
for −. The output is the triple of H, its distance matrix and the new
family. The partial graph is on `Fin n`, so |G| = n. M is
`maxTreeSize G k q`, the time is `O(n² · (M + T + 1)^a)`, and each new
tree has an encoding of length at most `c · (T + 1)^a`, where the degree
`a` and the constant `c` may depend on k and q. The second factor of
the time is increased by one, so that it is positive. The set in the
definition of T collects trees of G of tuples from balls in H.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax185574.TypeTrees
import Lax185574.ConstructionSequences
import Lax185574.DistanceMatrix
import Lax185574.Algorithms

/-!
---
title: Lifting type trees through a resolve
type: lemma
---
Let k ≥ 1 and q ∈ ℕ. Given a partial graph G, its distance matrix D_G,
colors P, Q, a sign ±, and (tree^G_{k,q}(a) : a ∈ V(G)), one can compute
H = resolve^±_{P,Q}(G), its distance matrix D_H, and
(tree^H_{k,q}(a) : a ∈ V(G)) in time

  |G|² · poly_{k,q}(M + T),

where

  M = max_{a ∈ V(G)} ‖tree^G_{k,q}(a)‖,
  T = max_{a ∈ V(G)} |{tree^G_{k+i,q−i}(v̄) | 0 ≤ i ≤ q, ℓ ∈ [k+i],
                       v̄ ∈ (Ball^H_{ρ⁺(k,q)}(a))^ℓ}|.

Each output tree has size poly_{k,q}(T).

# Formalization notes

The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`,
one for all k and q. Its input is the tuple of G, its distance matrix,
P, Q, the sign and the family of type trees, with the encodings of
`Lax185574.Encodings`. The sign is a Boolean, `true` for + and `false`
for −. The output is the triple of H, its distance matrix and the new
family. The partial graph is on `Fin n`, so |G| = n. M is
`maxTreeSize G k q`, the time is `O(n² · (M + T + 1)^a)`, and each new
tree has an encoding of length at most `c · (T + 1)^a`, where the degree

the time is increased by one, so that it is positive. The set in the
definition of T collects trees of G of tuples from balls in H.
-/

namespace Lax185574.ResolveLift

open Lax185574.Encoding Lax185574.Algorithms
open Lax185574.PartialGraphs Lax185574.TypeTrees Lax185574.ConstructionSequences
open Lax185574.DistanceMatrix
open Lax3.DistFO (rhoMinus rhoPlus)

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- `resolve^±_{P,Q}(G)`, positive for `true`. -/
def resolveBy (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (s : Bool) (P Q : ℕ) : PartialGraph (Fin n) :=
  if s then resolvePos G P Q else resolveNeg G P Q

/-- The parameter `T`: the largest number of type trees in `G` of
tuples from a ball of radius `ρ⁺(k, q)` in `H`, over all ranks
`(k+i, q−i)` and arities `ℓ ∈ [k+i]`. -/
noncomputable def treeCount (G H : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (k q : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun a : Fin n =>
    Set.ncard {τ : TypeTree | ∃ (i ℓ : ℕ) (v : Fin ℓ → Fin n), i ≤ q ∧ 1 ≤ ℓ ∧ ℓ ≤ k + i ∧
      (∀ j, v j ∈ H.ball (rhoPlus k q) a) ∧ τ = tree G (k + i) (q - i) v}

/-- **Resolve lift.** One algorithm computes the partial graph `H` after
a resolve, its distance matrix and the type trees of all vertices in it,
from the partial graph `G` before, its distance matrix, `P`, `Q`, the
sign and its type trees, in time `O(n² · (M + T + 1)^a)`. Each new tree
has size `O((T + 1)^a)`. -/
axiom exists_program_resolveLift :
    ∃ A : Algorithm, ∀ k q : ℕ, ∃ c a : ℕ,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (P Q : ℕ) (s : Bool), 1 ≤ k →
        let H := resolveBy G s P Q
        let T := treeCount G H k q
        A.Computes c (G, distMatrix G, P, Q, s, family G k q) (H, distMatrix H, family H k q)
            (n ^ 2 * (maxTreeSize G k q + T + 1) ^ a) ∧
          ∀ b : Fin n, (encode (tree H k q ![b])).length ≤ c * (T + 1) ^ a

end Lax185574.ResolveLift

statements.signature:
exists_program_resolveLift : Exists fun A =>
  ∀ (k q : Nat),
    Exists fun c =>
      Exists fun a =>
        ∀ (n : Nat) (G : Lax185574.PartialGraphs.PartialGraph (Fin n)) (P Q : Nat) (s : Bool),
          instLENat.le 1 k →
            let H := Lax185574.ResolveLift.resolveBy G s P Q;
            let T := Lax185574.ResolveLift.treeCount G H k q;
            And
              (A.Computes c
                { fst := G,
                  snd :=
                    { fst := Lax185574.DistanceMatrix.distMatrix G,
                      snd :=
                        { fst := P,
                          snd := { fst := Q, snd := { fst := s, snd := Lax185574.TypeTrees.family G k q } } } } }
                { fst := H,
                  snd := { fst := Lax185574.DistanceMatrix.distMatrix H, snd := Lax185574.TypeTrees.family H k q } }
                (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow n.cast 2)
                  (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax185574.TypeTrees.maxTreeSize G k q).cast T.cast) 1)
                    a)))
              (∀ (b : Fin n),
                instLENat.le
                  (Lax185574.TypeTrees.instEncodeTypeTree.encode
                      (Lax185574.TypeTrees.tree H k q (Matrix.vecCons b Matrix.vecEmpty))).length
                  (instHMul.hMul c (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd T 1) a)))

**Resolve lift.** One algorithm computes the partial graph `H` after
a resolve, its distance matrix and the type trees of all vertices in it,
from the partial graph `G` before, its distance matrix, `P`, `Q`, the
sign and its type trees, in time `O(n² · (M + T + 1)^a)`. Each new tree
has size `O((T + 1)^a)`.

concepts.title: Ordered coordinate restriction of type trees
concepts.description:
There is an operation ↾ on type trees such that for all k, q ∈ ℕ,
partial graphs G, tuples w̄ ∈ V(G)^ℓ with ℓ ≤ k and ordered lists J of
distinct positions in [ℓ],

  tree_{k,q}(w̄) ↾ J = tree_{k,q}(w̄ ↾ J).

Given τ and J one can compute τ ↾ J in time polynomial in ‖τ‖.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The operation is given by one algorithm in the sense of
`Lax185574.Algorithms`, for all k and q. Its input is the pair of the
tree and J, a list of positions. Positions are counted from 0. The tuple
w̄ ↾ J has the entries w_{j₁}, …, w_{j_p}. The size ‖τ‖ is the length of
the encoding of τ, and the time is `O((‖τ‖ + 1)^a)`, where the degree
`a` and the constant `c` may depend on k and q. The paper says
polynomial time, with no subscript, so this is weaker than a degree
independent of k and q. It suffices, since k and q are fixed in every
use.

import Lax185574.TypeTrees
import Lax185574.Algorithms

/-!
---
title: Ordered coordinate restriction of type trees
type: lemma
---
There is an operation ↾ on type trees such that for all k, q ∈ ℕ,
partial graphs G, tuples w̄ ∈ V(G)^ℓ with ℓ ≤ k and ordered lists J of
distinct positions in [ℓ],

  tree_{k,q}(w̄) ↾ J = tree_{k,q}(w̄ ↾ J).

Given τ and J one can compute τ ↾ J in time polynomial in ‖τ‖.

# Formalization notes

The operation is given by one algorithm in the sense of
`Lax185574.Algorithms`, for all k and q. Its input is the pair of the
tree and J, a list of positions. Positions are counted from 0. The tuple
w̄ ↾ J has the entries w_{j₁}, …, w_{j_p}. The size ‖τ‖ is the length of
the encoding of τ, and the time is `O((‖τ‖ + 1)^a)`, where the degree
`a` and the constant `c` may depend on k and q. The paper says
polynomial time, with no subscript, so this is weaker than a degree
independent of k and q. It suffices, since k and q are fixed in every
use.
-/

namespace Lax185574.Restriction

open Lax185574.Encoding Lax185574.Algorithms
open Lax185574.PartialGraphs Lax185574.TypeTrees

/-- **Ordered coordinate restriction.** One algorithm computes
`tree_{k,q}(u ↾ J)` from `tree_{k,q}(u)` and `J`, in time polynomial in
the size of the tree. -/
axiom exists_program_restrict :
    ∃ A : Algorithm, ∀ k q : ℕ, ∃ c a : ℕ,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (ℓ : ℕ) (u : Fin ℓ → Fin n) (J : List (Fin ℓ)),
        ℓ ≤ k → J.Nodup →
          A.Computes c (tree G k q u, J) (tree G k q (fun i => u (J.get i)))
            (((encode (tree G k q u)).length + 1) ^ a)

end Lax185574.Restriction

statements.signature:
exists_program_restrict : Exists fun A =>
  ∀ (k q : Nat),
    Exists fun c =>
      Exists fun a =>
        ∀ (n : Nat) (G : Lax185574.PartialGraphs.PartialGraph (Fin n)) (ℓ : Nat) (u : Fin ℓ → Fin n) (J : List (Fin ℓ)),
          instLENat.le ℓ k →
            J.Nodup →
              A.Computes c { fst := Lax185574.TypeTrees.tree G k q u, snd := J }
                (Lax185574.TypeTrees.tree G k q fun i => u (J.get i))
                (instHPow.hPow
                  (instHAdd.hAdd
                    (Lax185574.TypeTrees.instEncodeTypeTree.encode (Lax185574.TypeTrees.tree G k q u)).length.cast 1)
                  a)

concepts.title: Scatter types
concepts.description:
Let G be a partial graph. A set S of vertices is *r-scattered* if all
vertices of S have pairwise distance larger than r. Fix a linear order
on V(G). For X ⊆ V(G) and r ∈ ℕ, S_r(X) is the inclusion-wise maximal
r-scattered subset of X built by the greedy process that repeatedly adds
the least available vertex.

The *(k, q)-scatter type* stp^G_{k,q} is the function with domain

  {(r, tree_{k+i,q−i}(b)) | i ∈ [q], b ∈ V(G),
   r ∈ [9^{k+i} · ρ⁻(k+i, q−i)]}

given by stp^G_{k,q}(r, ν) = min(|S_r([ν]^G)|, k + q). For q = 0 the
domain is empty. A scatter type is represented canonically as the sorted
list of its triples (r, ν, stp_{k,q}(r, ν)), using the canonical
representation of ν. Its size ‖stp_{k,q}‖ is the size of this list.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The vertices are `Fin n`, ordered as numbers. The greedy process scans
the vertices in increasing order and adds a vertex of X when its
distance to every vertex added so far is larger than r. [k] = {1, …, k}
as in the paper, so i and r start at 1. The domain of stp^G_{k,q},
written domain(stp_{k,q}) in the paper, is `domain G k q`.

The scatter type is given by its graph, the finite set of the pairs
((r, ν), stp_{k,q}(r, ν)) with (r, ν) in its domain. As a finite set it is
encoded as the sorted list of the words of these pairs, by
`Lax185574.Encodings`. The word of a pair is r, then the word of ν,
then the value.

import Lax185574.TypeTrees
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange

/-!
---
title: Scatter types
type: definition
---
Let G be a partial graph. A set S of vertices is *r-scattered* if all
vertices of S have pairwise distance larger than r. Fix a linear order
on V(G). For X ⊆ V(G) and r ∈ ℕ, S_r(X) is the inclusion-wise maximal
r-scattered subset of X built by the greedy process that repeatedly adds
the least available vertex.

The *(k, q)-scatter type* stp^G_{k,q} is the function with domain

  {(r, tree_{k+i,q−i}(b)) | i ∈ [q], b ∈ V(G),
   r ∈ [9^{k+i} · ρ⁻(k+i, q−i)]}

given by stp^G_{k,q}(r, ν) = min(|S_r([ν]^G)|, k + q). For q = 0 the
domain is empty. A scatter type is represented canonically as the sorted
list of its triples (r, ν, stp_{k,q}(r, ν)), using the canonical
representation of ν. Its size ‖stp_{k,q}‖ is the size of this list.

# Formalization notes

The vertices are `Fin n`, ordered as numbers. The greedy process scans
the vertices in increasing order and adds a vertex of X when its
distance to every vertex added so far is larger than r. [k] = {1, …, k}
as in the paper, so i and r start at 1. The domain of stp^G_{k,q},
written domain(stp_{k,q}) in the paper, is `domain G k q`.

The scatter type is given by its graph, the finite set of the pairs
((r, ν), stp_{k,q}(r, ν)) with (r, ν) in its domain. As a finite set it is
encoded as the sorted list of the words of these pairs, by
`Lax185574.Encodings`. The word of a pair is r, then the word of ν,
then the value.
-/

namespace Lax185574.ScatterTypes

open Lax185574.PartialGraphs Lax185574.GaifmanGraph
open Lax185574.TypeTrees
open Lax3.DistFO (rhoMinus rhoPlus)

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- `S_r(X)`: the greedy maximal `r`-scattered subset of `X`, scanning
the vertices in increasing order. -/
noncomputable def greedyScattered (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (r : ℕ) (X : Set (Fin n)) :
    List (Fin n) :=
  open Classical in
  (List.finRange n).foldl
    (fun S v => if v ∈ X ∧ ∀ u ∈ S, ¬ WithinDist G.resolved r u v then S ++ [v] else S) []

/-- The domain `domain(stp_{k,q})` of the scatter type. -/
def domain (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (k q : ℕ) : Set (ℕ × TypeTree) :=
  {p | ∃ (i : ℕ) (b : Fin n), 1 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ q ∧ 1 ≤ p.1 ∧
    p.1 ≤ 9 ^ (k + i) * rhoMinus (k + i) (q - i) ∧
    p.2 = tree G (k + i) (q - i) ![b]}

/-- The value `min(|S_r([ν]^G)|, k + q)` at the pair `p = (r, ν)`. -/
noncomputable def value (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (k q : ℕ) (p : ℕ × TypeTree) : ℕ :=
  min (greedyScattered G p.1 (realizations G p.2)).length (k + q)

/-- The graph `{(x, f x) | x ∈ D}` of a function on a finite domain. -/
noncomputable def graphOn {α β : Type*} (D : Set α) (f : α → β) : Finset (α × β) :=
  finsetOf {p | p.1 ∈ D ∧ p.2 = f p.1}

/-- `stp^G_{k,q}`, as its graph: the pairs `((r, ν), stp(r, ν))` with
`(r, ν) ∈ domain(stp_{k,q})`. -/
noncomputable def stp (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (k q : ℕ) : Finset ((ℕ × TypeTree) × ℕ) :=
  graphOn (domain G k q) (value G k q)

end Lax185574.ScatterTypes

concepts.title: Few types far from a parameter set
concepts.description:
For every q, k, c ∈ ℕ there are numbers r = r(q) and T = T(q, k, c)
with the following property. Let H be a graph expanded by at most c
unary predicates and U ⊆ V(H). Consider the set

  F ≔ { a ∈ V(H) : dist^H(a, U) > r }

of vertices that are far from U. Then |Types^H_{k,q}(F/U)| ≤ T(q, k, c).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The radius r is quantified after q and before k and c, and T after
q, k and c. In particular neither depends on the graph or on |U|. An
expansion by at most c unary predicates is an expansion by exactly c
color sets, some of which may be empty, as in `Colorings.expansion`.
The graph is finite, which is the case in which the lemma is used. The
distance is that of the graph H, which is also the distance in the
Gaifman graph of the expansion. The far set F is the complement of
the ball Ball^H_r[U] of `GraphBalls.graphBall`, so a vertex lies in F if
no walk of length at most r joins a vertex of U to it. If U is empty, F
is the whole vertex set.

concepts.title: Few types far from a parameter set, with a fixed tuple of parameters
concepts.description:
For every q, k, c ∈ ℕ there are numbers r = r(q) and T = T(q, k, c)
with the following property. Let H be a graph expanded by at most c
unary predicates and U ⊆ V(H). Fix a tuple ū of vertices of U of finite
length. Let F ≔ { a ∈ V(H) : dist^H(a, U) > r }. Then

  |{ tp^H_q(ā ū/U) : ā ∈ F^k }| ≤ T(q, k, c).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The quantifier order is that of `SeparatingTypes`: r depends on q only,
and T on q, k and c only. In particular T does not depend on the length
m of ū. The tuple ā ū is the concatenation `Fin.append ā ū` of length
k + m. The far set F is the complement of the ball Ball^H_r[U] of
`GraphBalls.graphBall`. As in `SeparatingTypes`, the graph
is finite and its expansion has exactly c, possibly empty, color sets.

concepts.title: Splitting by a transversal keeps few parts in flip-metric balls
concepts.description:
Let G be a graph, 𝒫 ≼ 𝒬 partitions of V(G), and T a transversal of 𝒫.
Suppose |Ball^𝒬_{r+1}(v)/𝒫| ≤ k for every v ∈ V(G). Then for every
v ∈ V(G),

|Ball^𝒬_r(v)/(𝒫 ∧ T)| ≤ k · π_G(k).

This is Corollary 5.4 of Drabik, Dumas, Geniet, Nowakowski, Pilipczuk and
Toruńczyk, *Variants of merge-width and applications* (2026).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The balls are those of the 𝒬-flip metric, `Flips.flipBall`, and 𝒫 ∧ T
is `TypeSplitting.split`. The neighborhood complexity π_G is
`VCDimension.neighborhoodComplexity`. The graph is finite, so that the
counts of parts are exact. The radius r and the bound k are arbitrary
natural numbers.

concepts.title: Splitting by minimal representatives preserves coarsening
concepts.description:
Fix a graph G together with a total order < on its vertices. Let
𝒫₁ ≼ 𝒫₂ ≼ ⋯ ≼ 𝒫_m be a sequence of ever coarser partitions of V(G). Pick
representatives T₁ ⊇ T₂ ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ T_m of 𝒫₁, …, 𝒫_m by setting

T_i ≔ { min_<(P) : P ∈ 𝒫_i },

and define 𝒬_i ≔ 𝒫_i ∧ T_i. Then 𝒬₁ ≼ 𝒬₂ ≼ ⋯ ≼ 𝒬_m is also a sequence
of ever coarser partitions.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The paper uses this lemma inside the proof that the partitions of its
merge sequence get coarser.

The order is a linear order on the vertex type. The set T_i is the set
of vertices that are minimal in their part, `minimalVertices`. On a
finite vertex type every part has a minimum, so this set is a
transversal. The conclusion needs no finiteness. The sequence is a
list, and the hypothesis and the conclusion compare consecutive
entries.

def minimalVertices [LinearOrder V] (P : Setoid V) : Set V :=
  {v | ∀ u : V, P u v → v ≤ u}

/-- **Coarsening is preserved.** Splitting ever coarser partitions
along their minimal vertices gives ever coarser partitions. -/

    (h : ∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : t + 1 < Ps.length), Ps[t] ≤ Ps[t + 1]) :
    ∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : t + 1 < Ps.length),
      split G Ps[t] (minimalVertices Ps[t]) ≤ split G Ps[t + 1] (minimalVertices Ps[t + 1])

end Lax185574.SplittingMonotone

concepts.title: Computing the far tree
concepts.description:
Fix k ∈ ℕ and q ≥ 1, let G be a partial graph, and let ā ∈ V(G)^{≤k} be
nonempty. Then ftree_{k,q}(ā) is computable from tree_{k,q}(ā) and
stp_{k,q} in time

  ‖stp_{k,q}‖ · poly_{k,q}(‖tree_{k,q}(ā)‖).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The algorithm is an algorithm in the sense of `Lax185574.Algorithms`,
one for all k and q. q ≥ 1 is written as q + 1. The input is the pair of
the type tree and the scatter type. Sizes are lengths of encodings. The
time is `O((‖stp‖ + 1) · (‖τ‖ + 1)^a)`, where the degree `a` and the
constant `c` may depend on k and q. The factors are increased by one, so
that the bound is positive.

from `tree_{k,q}(u)` and `stp_{k,q}`, in time linear in the size of the

concepts.title: Type trees are distance types
concepts.description:
Fix ℓ ≤ k and q, a partial graph G and ā, b̄ ∈ V(G)^ℓ. Then
tree_{k,q}(ā) = tree_{k,q}(b̄) if and only if G ⊨ φ(ā) ⇔ φ(b̄) for every
distFO formula φ(x̄) of distance rank (k, q) with |x̄| = ℓ.

trees is equality of the objects of `Lax185574.TypeTrees`.

/-- **Type trees are distance types.** Two tuples have the same type

concepts.title: Locality of type trees
concepts.description:
Every node at depth j of tree_{k,q}(a) is tree_{k+j,q−j}(v̄) for some
tuple v̄ from Ball_{ρ⁺(k,q)}(a), and every color mentioned in the root
label of that node intersects this ball.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
By the definition of extensions, the nodes at depth j of tree_{k,q}(a)
are the trees tree_{k+j,q−j}(v̄) of the tuples v̄ = (v₀, …, v_j) with
v₀ = a in which every vᵢ with i ≥ 1 is within distance ρ⁺(k+i, q−i) of
an earlier entry. The statement is made for these tuples. The root label
of the node is atp_{k+j,q−j}(v̄), which consists of the atoms that hold.
An atom mentions the color Y if it is Y(xᵢ) or dist(xᵢ, Y) < r.

The paper assumes k ≥ 1, so that the single vertex a has a tree of
rank (k, q). The statement about guarded tuples does not need this
hypothesis, and it holds for all k.

open Lax185574.DistanceLogic Lax185574.DistanceLogic.DistFO Lax185574.TypeTrees
open Lax3.DistFO (rhoMinus rhoPlus)

/-- The atom mentions the color `Y`. -/
def MentionsColor (Y : ℕ) {ℓ : ℕ} : DistFO ℓ → Prop
  | .color Y' _ => Y' = Y
  | .distColorLt _ Y' _ => Y' = Y
  | _ => False

/-- **Locality of type trees.** A tuple reached from `v 0` by guarded
extensions lies in the ball of radius `ρ⁺(k, q)` around `v 0`, and so
does a vertex of every color mentioned in its atomic type. -/
axiom ball_of_guarded {V : Type*} (G : PartialGraph V) (k q j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ q)
    (v : Fin (j + 1) → V)
    (hv : ∀ i : Fin (j + 1), 0 < i.val → ∃ i' : Fin (j + 1), i'.val < i.val ∧
      WithinDist G.resolved (rhoPlus (k + i.val) (q - i.val)) (v i') (v i)) :
    (∀ i, v i ∈ G.ball (rhoPlus k q) (v 0)) ∧
    ∀ φ ∈ atp G (k + j) (q - j) v, ∀ Y : ℕ, MentionsColor Y φ →
      ∃ u ∈ G.ball (rhoPlus k q) (v 0), G.color u = Y

end Lax185574.TreeLocality

                (Lax185574.GaifmanGraph.WithinDist G.resolved
                  (Lax3.DistFO.rhoPlus (instHAdd.hAdd k i.val) (instHSub.hSub q i.val)) (v i') (v i))) →
        And (∀ (i : Fin (instHAdd.hAdd j 1)), Set.instMembership.mem (G.ball (Lax3.DistFO.rhoPlus k q) (v 0)) (v i))
          (∀ (φ : Lax185574.DistanceLogic.DistFO (instHAdd.hAdd j 1)),
            Set.instMembership.mem (Lax185574.TypeTrees.atp G (instHAdd.hAdd k j) (instHSub.hSub q j) v) φ →

concepts.title: Polynomial bound on the number of types over a parameter set
concepts.description:
Let 𝒞 be a monadically dependent graph class and k, q, c ∈ ℕ. For every
graph G ∈ 𝒞, every expansion G⁺ of G by c unary predicates and every
subset U ⊆ V(G),

|Types^{G⁺}_{k,q}(V(G)/U)| ≤ O_{𝒞,q,k,c}(1) · poly_{𝒞,q,k}(|U|).

The degree of the polynomial does not depend on the number c of unary
predicates. Only the constant factor does.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The bound is spelled out: there is an exponent `a`, depending on the
class, `k` and `q`, and for each `c` a factor `F`, such that the count is
at most `F · (|U| + 1)^a`. The quantifier order puts `a` before `c`,
which is the uniformity in the number of colors that the theorem is
about. The paper proves the statement for possibly infinite graphs with
finite U. Here it is stated for the finite graphs of a `GraphClass`,
which is the case the model-checking theorem uses.

/-!
---
title: Polynomial bound on the number of types over a parameter set
type: theorem
---
Let 𝒞 be a monadically dependent graph class and k, q, c ∈ ℕ. For every
graph G ∈ 𝒞, every expansion G⁺ of G by c unary predicates and every
subset U ⊆ V(G),

|Types^{G⁺}_{k,q}(V(G)/U)| ≤ O_{𝒞,q,k,c}(1) · poly_{𝒞,q,k}(|U|).

The degree of the polynomial does not depend on the number c of unary
predicates. Only the constant factor does.

# Formalization notes

The bound is spelled out: there is an exponent `a`, depending on the
class, `k` and `q`, and for each `c` a factor `F`, such that the count is
at most `F · (|U| + 1)^a`. The quantifier order puts `a` before `c`,
which is the uniformity in the number of colors that the theorem is
about. The paper proves the statement for possibly infinite graphs with
finite U. Here it is stated for the finite graphs of a `GraphClass`,
which is the case the model-checking theorem uses.
-/

namespace Lax185574.TypeBound

open Lax185574.Graphs Lax185574.MonadicDependence
open Lax185574.FirstOrderTypes Lax185574.Colorings

/-- **Type bound.** In a monadically dependent class, the number of
types of quantifier rank `q` of `k`-tuples over a parameter set `U`, in
an expansion by `c` unary predicates, is at most `F · (|U| + 1)^a`. The
exponent `a` does not depend on `c`. -/
axiom typeCountOver_le (C : GraphClass) (hC : MonadicallyDependent C)
    (k q : ℕ) :
    ∃ a : ℕ, ∀ c : ℕ, ∃ F : ℕ, ∀ G ∈ C,
      ∀ (colors : Fin c → Set (Fin G.n)) (U : Finset (Fin G.n)),
        typeCountOver (expansion G.toSimpleGraph colors) k q Set.univ (U : Set (Fin G.n)) ≤
          F * (U.card + 1) ^ a

end Lax185574.TypeBound

  Lax185574.MonadicDependence.MonadicallyDependent C →
    ∀ (k q : Nat),

        ∀ (c : Nat),
          Exists fun F =>
            ∀ (G : Lax185574.Graphs.Graph),
              Set.instMembership.mem C G →
                ∀ (colors : Fin c → Set (Fin G.n)) (U : Finset (Fin G.n)),
                  instLENat.le

                      Set.univ (Finset.instSetLike.coe U))
                    (instHMul.hMul F (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd U.card 1) a))

concepts.title: Splitting the parts of a partition by atomic types over a set
concepts.description:
Fix a graph G and a partition 𝒫 of V(G). For a set T ⊆ V(G), 𝒫 ∧ T is
the refinement of 𝒫 where each part P ∈ 𝒫 is split into atomic types
over T ∖ P, that is, into sets of the form P ∩ Q, where Q is the set of
all vertices of G with a given neighborhood in T ∖ P.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The partition 𝒫 ∧ T is the kernel of the map sending v to its part
𝒫(v) together with N(v) ∩ (T ∖ 𝒫(v)). Two vertices have the same image
exactly when they lie in the same part P and have the same neighborhood
in T ∖ P, which is the description of the paper. A vertex of P does not
lie in T ∖ P, so its atomic type over T ∖ P is given by this
neighborhood alone. If 𝒫 has a single part, then T ∖ P is empty and
𝒫 ∧ T = 𝒫.

title: Splitting the parts of a partition by atomic types over a set
type: definition

# Formalization notes

The partition 𝒫 ∧ T is the kernel of the map sending v to its part
𝒫(v) together with N(v) ∩ (T ∖ 𝒫(v)). Two vertices have the same image
exactly when they lie in the same part P and have the same neighborhood
in T ∖ P, which is the description of the paper. A vertex of P does not

-/

namespace Lax185574.TypeSplitting

universe z

variable {V : Type z}

/-- `𝒫 ∧ T`: each part `P` of `P` is split according to the
neighborhoods of its vertices in `T ∖ P`. -/
def split (G : SimpleGraph V) (P : Setoid V) (T : Set V) : Setoid V :=
  Setoid.ker fun v => (Quotient.mk P v, {t | t ∈ T ∧ ¬ P t v} ∩ G.neighborSet v)

end Lax185574.TypeSplitting

concepts.title: Type trees and their canonical representation
concepts.description:
Let G be a partial graph, k, q ∈ ℕ and ā a tuple of ℓ vertices. The
*atomic (k, q)-type* atp_{k,q}(ā) is the set of atomic distFO formulas
of distance rank (k, q) with free variables among x₁, …, x_ℓ that ā
satisfies in G. The *(k, q)-type tree* of ā is

  tree_{k,q}(ā) = (atp_{k,q}(ā), 𝓔_{k,q}(ā)),

where 𝓔_{k,0}(ā) = ∅ and, for q ≥ 1,

  𝓔_{k,q}(ā) = {(i, tree_{k+1,q−1}(ā b)) | i ∈ [ℓ], b ∈ V(G),
                 dist(aᵢ, b) ≤ ρ⁺(k+1, q−1)}.

The members of 𝓔_{k,q}(ā) are the *extensions*, and i is the *guard*
of the extension. The number ℓ is the *arity* and (k, q) is the *rank*
of the tree.

Type trees are represented on the RAM in a canonical form, with all sets
sorted and free of duplicates, so that two trees are equal exactly when
their representations are. The size ‖τ‖ of a tree is the size of its
representation, which includes k, q and ℓ.

For a type tree ν of arity one, [ν]^G is the set of vertices b with
tree_{k,q}(b) = ν, where (k, q) is the rank of ν.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A type tree is a Lean object of type `TypeTree`. It records its rank
(k, q), its arity ℓ and its root, an element of `Node q ℓ`. A root of
depth 0 is its root label, the finite set of its atoms. A root of depth
q + 1 is its root label together with the finite set of its extensions,
pairs of a guard and a root of depth q and arity ℓ + 1. The trees inside
a tree carry no rank and arity, since these are determined by the
enclosing tree. Equality of type trees in the paper is equality of
these objects.

The canonical representation of a type tree is its encoding, in the
sense of `Lax185574.Encoding`. It is the header k, q, ℓ, followed by the
encoding of the set of atoms of the root and, at depth at least one, the
encoding of the set of extensions. An atom is encoded as a formula of
`Lax185574.DistanceLogic`, and an extension (i, μ) by i followed by the
encoding of μ. Finite sets are encoded sorted and without repetitions,
so the encoding is determined by the tree. The size ‖τ‖ is the length of
the encoding, `wordLength τ`. The operations of the paper are computed
by word RAM programs on these encodings.

The algorithms of the model-checking procedure receive and return the
family (tree_{k,q}(a) : a ∈ V(G)) of the type trees of all vertices of a
partial graph on `Fin n`. It is `family G k q`, a function on `Fin n`,
encoded as the list of its members in the order of the vertices.

Sets are turned into finite sets by `finsetOf`. On an infinite set it
returns the empty set. This case does not occur for partial graphs on a
finite vertex type, where all the sets involved are finite. In
particular, only finitely many colors occur, and an atom with a color
that does not occur is false.

pairs of a guard and a root of depth q and arity ℓ + 1. The trees inside
a tree carry no rank and arity, since these are determined by the
enclosing tree. Equality of type trees in the paper is equality of
these objects.

The canonical representation of a type tree is its encoding, in the
sense of `Lax185574.Encoding`. It is the header k, q, ℓ, followed by the
encoding of the set of atoms of the root and, at depth at least one, the
encoding of the set of extensions. An atom is encoded as a formula of
`Lax185574.DistanceLogic`, and an extension (i, μ) by i followed by the
encoding of μ. Finite sets are encoded sorted and without repetitions,
so the encoding is determined by the tree. The size ‖τ‖ is the length of
the encoding, `wordLength τ`. The operations of the paper are computed
by word RAM programs on these encodings.

The algorithms of the model-checking procedure receive and return the
family (tree_{k,q}(a) : a ∈ V(G)) of the type trees of all vertices of a
partial graph on `Fin n`. It is `family G k q`, a function on `Fin n`,
encoded as the list of its members in the order of the vertices.

Sets are turned into finite sets by `finsetOf`. On an infinite set it
returns the empty set. This case does not occur for partial graphs on a
finite vertex type, where all the sets involved are finite. In
particular, only finitely many colors occur, and an atom with a color
that does not occur is false.
-/

namespace Lax185574.TypeTrees

open Lax185574.PartialGraphs Lax185574.GaifmanGraph Lax185574.Encoding
open Lax185574.DistanceLogic Lax185574.DistanceLogic.DistFO
open Lax3.DistFO (rhoMinus rhoPlus)

/-- `Node q ℓ`: the roots of the type trees of depth `q` and arity `ℓ`.
A root of depth `0` is its set of atoms. A root of depth `q + 1` is its
set of atoms together with its set of extensions, pairs of a guard and
a root of depth `q` and arity `ℓ + 1`. -/
def Node : ℕ → ℕ → Type
  | 0, ℓ => Finset (DistFO ℓ)
  | q + 1, ℓ => Finset (DistFO ℓ) × Finset (Fin ℓ × Node q (ℓ + 1))

/-- A root of depth `0` is encoded by its set of atoms. A root of depth
`q + 1` is encoded by its set of atoms followed by its set of
extensions. `Node` is defined by recursion on the depth and is not an
inductive type, so its encoding is given by the same recursion. -/
@[instance_reducible] def Node.instEncode : (q ℓ : ℕ) → Encode (Node q ℓ)
  | 0, ℓ => inferInstanceAs (Encode (Finset (DistFO ℓ)))
  | q + 1, ℓ =>
      letI := Node.instEncode q (ℓ + 1)
      inferInstanceAs (Encode (Finset (DistFO ℓ) × Finset (Fin ℓ × Node q (ℓ + 1))))

instance {q ℓ : ℕ} : Encode (Node q ℓ) := Node.instEncode q ℓ

/-- A type tree: its rank `(k, q)`, its arity `ℓ` and its root. -/
structure TypeTree where
  /-- The first component of the rank. -/
  k : ℕ
  /-- The depth, the second component of the rank. -/
  q : ℕ
  /-- The arity. -/
  ℓ : ℕ
  /-- The root. -/
  root : Node q ℓ
  deriving Encode

variable {V : Type*}

/-- The finite set with the elements of `S`, and `∅` if `S` is
infinite. -/
noncomputable def finsetOf {α : Type*} (S : Set α) : Finset α :=
  open Classical in if h : S.Finite then h.toFinset else ∅

/-- `atp_{k,q}(a)`: the atoms of distance rank `(k, q)` satisfied by the
tuple `a`. -/
def atp (G : PartialGraph V) (k q : ℕ) {ℓ : ℕ} (a : Fin ℓ → V) : Set (DistFO ℓ) :=
  {φ | IsAtom φ ∧ DRank k q φ ∧ Sat G a φ}

/-- The root of `tree_{k,q}(a)`: the atoms of `atp_{k,q}(a)` and, for
`q ≥ 1`, the extensions `(i, tree_{k+1,q−1}(a b))`. -/
noncomputable def node (G : PartialGraph V) : (k q : ℕ) → {ℓ : ℕ} → (Fin ℓ → V) → Node q ℓ
  | k, 0, _, a => finsetOf (atp G k 0 a)
  | k, q + 1, ℓ, a =>
      (finsetOf (atp G k (q + 1) a),
       finsetOf {e | ∃ (i : Fin ℓ) (b : V),
          WithinDist G.resolved (rhoPlus (k + 1) q) (a i) b ∧
          e = (i, node G (k + 1) q (Fin.snoc a b))})

/-- `tree_{k,q}(a)`. -/
noncomputable def tree (G : PartialGraph V) (k q : ℕ) {ℓ : ℕ} (a : Fin ℓ → V) : TypeTree :=
  ⟨k, q, ℓ, node G k q a⟩

/-- `[ν]^G`: the vertices whose type tree is `ν`. The rank is read off
`ν`, which records it. -/
def realizations (G : PartialGraph V) (ν : TypeTree) : Set V :=
  {b | tree G ν.k ν.q ![b] = ν}

/-- The family `(tree_{k,q}(a) : a ∈ V(G))` of the type trees of all
vertices. -/
noncomputable def family {n : ℕ} (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (k q : ℕ) : Fin n → TypeTree :=
  fun a => tree G k q ![a]

/-- The largest size of a tree of the family. -/
noncomputable def maxTreeSize {n : ℕ} (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (k q : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun a : Fin n => wordLength (family G k q a)

end Lax185574.TypeTrees

concepts.title: Type tree sizes
concepts.description:
Let k ≥ 1 and q ∈ ℕ, and put r = ρ⁺(k, q) and d = r + k + q. The
following holds for every partial graph G.

1. |{tree^G_{k+i,q−i}(v̄) | v̄ ∈ X^ℓ}| ≤ |Types^G_{d,d}(X)| for all
   i ∈ {0, …, q}, ℓ ∈ [k+i] and X ⊆ V(G).
2. ‖tree^G_{k,q}(a)‖ ≤ poly_{k,q}(|Types^G_{d,d}(Ball^G_r(a))|) for every
   a ∈ V(G).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Types^G_{d,d}(X) is counted by `Lax185574.Width.partialTypeCount`, the
number of first-order types of quantifier rank d of d-tuples from X in
the partial graph G. The vertices are `Fin n`. The polynomial of the
second part has a constant and a degree depending on k and q.

namespace Lax185574.TypeTreeSizes

open Lax185574.PartialGraphs Lax185574.Encoding Lax185574.TypeTrees Lax185574.Width
open Lax3.DistFO (rhoMinus rhoPlus)

/-- **Type tree sizes, counting.** The number of type trees of tuples
from `X` is at most the number of `d`-types of `d`-tuples from `X`. -/
axiom treeCount_le {n : ℕ} (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (k q : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k)
    (i ℓ : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ q) (hℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ) (hℓk : ℓ ≤ k + i) (X : Set (Fin n)) :
    Set.ncard {τ : TypeTree | ∃ v : Fin ℓ → Fin n, (∀ j, v j ∈ X) ∧ τ = tree G (k + i) (q - i) v} ≤
      partialTypeCount G (rhoPlus k q + k + q) (rhoPlus k q + k + q) X

/-- **Type tree sizes, size.** The size of the type tree of a vertex is
polynomial in the number of `d`-types of `d`-tuples from its ball. -/
axiom tree_length_le (k q : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    ∃ c a : ℕ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : PartialGraph (Fin n)) (v : Fin n),
      wordLength (tree G k q ![v]) ≤
        c * (partialTypeCount G (rhoPlus k q + k + q) (rhoPlus k q + k + q)
          (G.ball (rhoPlus k q) v) + 1) ^ a

end Lax185574.TypeTreeSizes

concepts.title: Neighborhood complexity and VC-dimension
concepts.description:
The *neighborhood complexity* of a graph G is the function π_G : ℕ → ℕ
defined by

π_G(k) ≔ max_{S ⊆ V(G), |S| ≤ k} |{ N^G(v) ∩ S : v ∈ V(G) }|,

which counts the maximum number of distinct neighborhoods of vertices of
G restricted to a set of size at most k.

The *VC-dimension* of a graph G is the maximal size of a set A ⊆ V(G)
such that { N(v) ∩ A : v ∈ V(G) } = 2^A.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The number of traces |{ N^G(v) ∩ S : v ∈ V(G) }| is `traceCount` of the
Sparsity Lectures submission (Lax199508), which is the cardinality of
the set of traces. For a finite set S the traces are subsets of S, so
there are at most 2^|S| of them and the count is exact. The maximum over
all S with |S| ≤ k is the supremum of a set of natural numbers bounded
by 2^k, so it is attained.

A set A is shattered if every subset B ⊆ A is the trace N(v) ∩ A of some
vertex v. The VC-dimension is the supremum of the sizes of the finite
shattered sets, an extended natural number. It is the maximum of the
paper whenever that exists, and ⊤ for a graph with arbitrarily large
shattered sets. "VC-dimension at most d" is `vcDim G ≤ d`.
